- **PM Gati Shakti**, highways and multimodal logistics can lower transport costs. Demand, domestic components, skills, R&D and export competitiveness support industry.
- EVs eliminate tailpipe emissions, but total benefit depends on electricity mix, battery sourcing/recycling and vehicle use. Public transport and walkability also reduce congestion; replacing every car with an EV alone does not.

topics.title: Gulf of Aden: chokepoints and maritime security
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Between **Yemen / Arabian Peninsula (north)** and **Somalia / Horn of Africa (south)**; **Djibouti** at western approach, **Arabian Sea** to east. **Socotra belongs to Yemen**, near the eastern approach.
- **Arabian Sea → Gulf of Aden → Bab el-Mandeb → Red Sea → Suez Canal → Mediterranean**. Gulf of Aden does not directly open into the Mediterranean.
- **Guardafui Channel**: between northeastern Somalia and Socotra; **Gulf of Tadjoura**: western inlet in Djibouti. **Hormuz** connects Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman, not Aden/Red Sea.
- Source dimensions roughly **900 km × 500 km**, area **410,000 km²**; approximate boundary-dependent measures. **Sheba Ridge**, active spreading system; salinity generally lower than the highly evaporative Red Sea.
- Ports/cities: **Aden, Mukalla, Ahwar, Balhaf (Yemen); Berbera, Bosaso (Somali coast); Djibouti City**.
## Security and economy
- Suez route vital for Asia–Europe commerce, energy and container shipping. Source **11% of seaborne petroleum** lacks a reference year/definition; avoid treating as an unchanging flow.
- Piracy, attacks on shipping and regional conflict threaten vessels and raise insurance/freight costs; diversions around the Cape lengthen voyages.
- Indian naval patrols, maritime-domain awareness, escorts/rescue and partner information-sharing; protect commerce while following international law and avoiding escalation.

topics.title: Lokpal: jurisdiction, composition and safeguards
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **Statutory**, not constitutional: **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**; commencement **16 January 2014**. First Foundation Day celebration **16 January 2025**, Delhi; commencement differs from first appointments.
- **Chairperson + up to eight members**; **50% judicial members**, **not less than 50% of members collectively from SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women**. Not a separate 50% quota for each group.
- Chair: former **CJI**, former **Supreme Court judge**, or eligible eminent person; judicial member: former **SC judge / High Court Chief Justice**. Eminent members require relevant expertise and statutory eligibility, not simply fame.
- **President** appoints on committee recommendation: **PM (chair), Lok Sabha Speaker, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition, CJI or nominated SC judge, eminent jurist**.
- **Five years or age 70**, whichever earlier; Chair remuneration equivalent to **CJI**, members to **SC judges**. [Act and sections](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2122?col=123456789%2F1362).
## Jurisdiction and exclusions
- Corruption offences under **Prevention of Corruption Act**: **PM, Union ministers, MPs, Central Groups A–D**, covered government-funded/controlled entities; qualifying foreign-contribution recipients above **₹10 lakh annually**.
- MPs' protected parliamentary speech/votes excluded; PM allegations concerning **international relations, external/internal security, public order, atomic energy and space** excluded.
- PM inquiry needs **full bench**, approval of **at least two-thirds**; in-camera proceedings and confidentiality safeguards apply. “PM entirely exempt” is incorrect.
- Complaint rules/form and statutory time limits apply; “any person may complain” does not mean every complaint is admissible regardless of content or age.
## Inquiry and powers
- Preliminary inquiry or investigation by authorised agency including **CBI**; **CVC route** for specified Central servant categories: Group **A/B** reports back to Lokpal; Group **C/D** proceeds under CVC powers with reporting/oversight.
- Lokpal supervises **CBI cases referred by it**, not every CBI case; investigating-officer transfer requires its approval in covered cases.
- Civil-court-type inquiry powers, searches, provisional attachment, record protection and recommendations for transfer/suspension. **Final confiscation is through Special Court**, not unrestricted direct Lokpal confiscation.
- Annual report to **President**, laid before **Parliament**; effectiveness needs staff, independent investigations, timely follow-up and due process.

topics.title: La Pérouse: multinational naval interoperability
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Exercise recall
- **French Navy-led multinational maritime exercise**, Indo-Pacific/Indian Ocean approaches; **INS Mumbai**, indigenous guided-missile destroyer, participated in January 2025.
- PIB labels 2025 **fourth edition**; French Navy release calls it **fifth**. Keep institutional discrepancy visible rather than silently settling it. [Indian Navy release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2093998&lang=2&reg=48), [French Navy account](https://www.defense.gouv.fr/marine/actualites/clemenceau-25-gan-lance-lexercice-multinational-perouse-25-detroits-reliant-oceans-indien).
- Source participants besides India: **France, Australia, UK, USA, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Canada**; not Russia. Nine nations including India.
- Maritime situational awareness, surveillance/interdiction, information-sharing and interoperability; surface/air defence, tactical manoeuvres, cross-deck landings and **VBSS: Visit, Board, Search and Seizure**.
- Supports **SAGAR: Security and Growth for All in the Region**, safe sea lanes and rules-based maritime cooperation; a naval exercise is not a bilateral trade agreement or binding alliance.

topics.title: IMEC: India–Middle East–Europe connectivity
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Proposed corridor
- **India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor**, MoU announced at **G20 New Delhi, September 2023**; **proposed ship-to-rail network**, not an already completed continuous rail route.
- **East corridor: India ↔ Arabian Gulf**; **Northern corridor: Gulf ↔ Europe**. Rail and maritime legs supplement existing sea/road routes, with planned **electricity/data cables and clean-hydrogen pipeline**.
- MoU participants: **India, USA, Saudi Arabia, UAE, EU, France, Germany, Italy**. **Jordan and Israel** appear on envisaged transit alignment but are not among the eight MoU participants. [Commerce Ministry parliamentary reply](https://commerce.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/LS-USQ-No.715-dt.-07.02.2024.pdf).
- **Practice-key correction:** shipping is integral. The PDF wrongly excludes maritime lanes while accepting cables/pipeline; its listed options lack the complete **A+B+D+E** combination. Nuclear plants are not a specified core component.
## Source map: indicative ports, not a final binding route
| Region | Source-listed nodes |
| --- | --- |
| India | **Mundra, Kandla/Deendayal (Gujarat); JNPT/JNPA (Navi Mumbai)** |
| UAE | **Fujairah, Jebel Ali, Abu Dhabi** |
| Saudi Arabia | **Dammam, Ras Al Khair** |
| Transit / Israel | Saudi Arabia → **Jordan → Haifa** |
| Europe | **Piraeus (Greece), Messina (Italy), Marseille (France)** |
- A particular map alignment is not proof every port or rail link was finalised in the founding MoU.
## Why it matters
- Diversified Asia–Europe trade, Gulf partnerships, port/logistics/manufacturing investment, possible SEZs, energy/digital links and jobs; geopolitical alternative to **BRI**, without implying every participant shares an anti-China alliance.
- Source **40% faster** and **US$3–8 bn cost** are estimates without a settled route/financial baseline, not guaranteed realised savings or a final whole-project budget.
- Potential “infrastructure for peace” needs actual diplomatic stability; prospective Africa extensions are not an existing IMEC leg.
## Challenges and way forward
- Missing rail links, port capacity and **ship↔rail transshipment**; customs documentation, gauges/technical standards, tariffs and multimodal scheduling.
- Financing, commercial viability, Israel–regional conflict, infrastructure protection, environmental impact and country-specific laws.
- Phase viable segments; agree interoperable systems and customs rules, transparent funding/risk allocation, resilient energy/data links and partner consultation. IMEC complements other routes rather than guaranteeing elimination of Suez traffic.

topics.title: Colonial wealth extraction and inequality
topics.subject: Modern Indian History
topics.markdown:
## Oxfam: Takers, Not Makers (2025)
- Report links inherited fortunes, colonial exploitation and contemporary global inequality; arguments/statistics belong to the **2025 report**, not a neutral audited historical cash ledger.
- Estimate of India→UK extraction **1765–1900: US$64.82 trillion**; **US$33.8 trillion**, roughly **52%**, attributed to Britain's richest **10%**.
- **Method matters**: estimates of historical drain are **cumulated to 2020** in dollar terms; not simply the amount actually transferred in nineteenth-century dollars. Methodology contrasts **US$1.925 trillion cumulated to 1947**. Results depend on assumptions and compounding. [Oxfam methodology](https://www.oxfamfrance.org/app/uploads/2025/01/Oxfam-Davos-2025-Methodology-Note.pdf).
- Illustration that elite share could cover London in £50 notes nearly four times is an analogy, not an additional independent measurement. [Oxfam report summary](https://laos.oxfam.org/latest/publications/takers-not-makers).
## Mechanisms and historical connection
- Colonial revenue extraction, land/resource control, trade rules and labour exploitation transferred surplus abroad; raw-material exports and unequal market access constrained domestic development.
- **East India Company** combined commercial power and political coercion; important precursor to multinational networks, without treating all modern corporations as legally identical colonial rulers.
- Connect to **drain-of-wealth critique**: domestic surplus used abroad rather than reinvested locally. Different historical scholars' estimates must retain their period/method labels.
## Contemporary debate
- Oxfam links Global South labour/resource extraction to profits accruing in Global North; distinguish historical influence from assuming every present transaction has the same colonial mechanism.
- Proposed responses: effective progressive/wealth taxation, fairer labour/trade rules, debt relief, institutional reform, acknowledgement/reparations.
- Mains: explain mechanisms and distributional effects, assess methodology, and compare remedies for feasibility and equity; do not present reparations proposals as enacted policy.

topics.title: H-1B visas and skilled migration
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 framework
- **US non-immigrant, employer-sponsored visa** for specialty occupations requiring a directly related specialised bachelor's degree or equivalent; IT, engineering, medicine, finance, education and architecture examples.
- Employer offers qualifying job, obtains **Department of Labor-certified Labor Condition Application (LCA)**, then files **Form I-129 with USCIS**; approved petition precedes consular visa processing where applicable. Petition approval, visa and permission to enter are distinct.
- Required pay is the **higher of actual or prevailing wage**, not a licence to underpay foreign workers.
- Annual regular cap **65,000**, plus **20,000 US advanced-degree exemption**; qualifying higher-education institutions, affiliated nonprofits and nonprofit/government research organisations can be cap-exempt. Not every government-related employer is exempt.
- When oversubscribed, January framework uses **beneficiary-centric selection**; selection is not approval. Initial stay generally **up to three years**, ordinarily **six years total**, with statutory exceptions/extensions in some permanent-residence cases.
- Eligible spouses/unmarried children **under 21**: **H-4**. Green-card application may be possible but is not automatic permanent residency or work permission for every dependent.
## Reforms and Indian interests
- H-1B modernisation rule effective **17 January 2025**: clarified specialty-occupation criteria, flexibility for qualifying research employment/entrepreneurs, stronger compliance and changes to F-1 transition provisions. Separate **2024 registration-integrity rule** introduced beneficiary-centric selection. [Official January rule](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-12-18/html/2024-29354.htm).
- These are January historical rules, not an application guide to today's fees/selection requirements.
- India: skilled careers, diaspora networks and remittances versus talent loss, employer dependence and long residency queues; IT-company deployment, talent retention and return opportunities matter.
- Wage suppression, displacement and misuse are policy concerns to evaluate with evidence, not proof every migrant displaces an American worker. Skills, compliance and domestic talent development complement mobility.
## Brain circulation: January 29 editorial
- **Brain drain**: loss of skilled people; **brain gain**: attracting/retaining talent; **brain circulation**: repeated movement and exchange of skills, capital, research and diaspora networks. Returning talent does not automatically offset shortages in the sending country.
- Visa restrictions can encourage firms to move work abroad, especially R&D; effects on domestic employment depend on firms, occupations and the wider economy. [Glennon research](https://www.nber.org/papers/w27538).
- Source research examples, study-specific rather than universal forecasts: **10 denied positions → about 8 hires abroad**; **1% lower initial H-1B employment → 10–20% more foreign hiring**. Editorial also cites H-1B wage growth **52% versus 39%, 2003–2021**, immigrant-founded share above half of US billion-dollar startups, and foreign-born share **up to 71% of Silicon Valley tech workers**; denominators/periods differ.
- Source innovation estimates: **10% more foreign STEM workers → native wages +0.5–0.6%, patents/person +0.3–0.7%**; immigrant college graduates +1 percentage point associated with patents/person +9–18%. These are research estimates, not proof every worker gains or that a 1% relative rise equals one percentage point.
- Balance innovation/productivity and job creation against sector-specific displacement, wage compliance, dependence in sensitive technology and domestic skill shortages.
- India: research clusters, predictable funding/IP rules, deep-tech capital, joint patents/research, skills matching, simpler OCI services and pension portability agreements. **Startup visa** is an editorial proposal; IndiaStack/UPI illustrate ecosystem capacity, not substitutes for laboratory research.
- Mains structure: define circulation → diaspora/return networks → institutional barriers → feasible reforms and measurable gains. Source's 250-word/15-mark prompt is coaching practice, not a verified PYQ.

topics.title: BRICS: members, partners and cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 expansion
- **Nigeria: ninth partner country**, January announcement; partner status is **not full membership**. Other eight: **Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan**. [Brazilian presidency](https://brics.br/en/news/nine-nations-announced-as-brics-partner-countries).
- Original **BRIC**: Brazil, Russia, India, China; first leaders' summit **2009**. South Africa invited **2010**, joined summit **2011** → BRICS.
- **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE** entered in 2024; **Indonesia** full-member announcement January 2025. Saudi Arabia's invitation/accession was reported inconsistently; source's unquestioned **11-member count** should not erase that distinction. **Argentina**, shown in its graphic, declined the invitation.
- Three pillars: **political/security; economic/financial; cultural/people-to-people**. Informal intergovernmental grouping, not a military alliance.
- Source **~40% population / 37.3% GDP** needs membership/date and **PPP versus nominal** labels; do not mix them as exact universal shares.
- India hosted **4th summit 2012, 8th 2016, 13th 2021**.
## Mains frame
- Global South voice, institutional reform, development finance and trade/payment cooperation; diverse interests and bilateral tensions constrain consensus.
- January newspaper reports **100% tariff threat** if BRICS undermines dollar dominance; a threat is not an imposed blanket tariff or proof a common BRICS currency exists.

topics.title: Indus Waters Treaty and dispute settlement
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Allocation: January 2025 treaty context
- Signed **19 September 1960, Karachi**: **Jawaharlal Nehru / Ayub Khan**, with World Bank facilitation after extended negotiations.
| Eastern rivers: India | Western rivers: Pakistan, subject to permitted Indian uses |
| --- | --- |
| **Ravi, Beas, Sutlej** | **Indus, Jhelum, Chenab** |
- Allocation concerns water-use rights, not transfer of territorial sovereignty over entire rivers. India may undertake specified domestic/non-consumptive/agricultural uses and hydropower/storage under annexure conditions.
- Source approximations **80% / 19.48%** relate to aggregate flow, not an invariant volumetric quota; **3.6 million acre-feet** permitted Indian storage is subject to categories/conditions.
- Run-of-river projects are permitted within design constraints; advance project information/notices matter. **Kishenganga: Jhelum tributary; Ratle: Chenab**.
## Article IX: questions, differences, disputes
- **Permanent Indus Commission**, one commissioner each, first examines questions.
- Specified technical **differences → Neutral Expert** under Annexure F; qualifying **disputes → negotiation/arbitration** under Annexure G. Not every case mechanically passes through three appellate courts; jurisdiction depends on subject and treaty procedure.
- World Bank has specified appointment responsibilities, **not general authority to decide every water dispute**. [Treaty text](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents.htm?dtl%2F6439%2FIndus=&outputType=chromeless).
## Dated procedure
- Pakistan requested Neutral Expert **2015**, sought arbitration **2016**; India sought Expert. World Bank paused parallel appointments **2016**, resumed both processes **2022**. [World Bank account](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/04/06/world-bank-resumes-processes-under-indus-waters-treaty).
- Source's **90-day modification notice / 62-year wording** refers to **January 2023**, not a newly issued January 2025 notice. **Article XII(3)** modification requires a **duly ratified treaty agreed by both governments**; notice alone does not amend it.
- January 2025 news: Neutral Expert decision **7 January**, public release **20 January**, on **competence** over technical issues; jurisdiction decision differs from final merits ruling. [PCA release](https://pca-cpa.org/en/news/pca-press-release-pca-case-no-2023-14-neutral-expert-issues-decision-on-certain-issues-pertaining-to-the-competence-of-the-neutral-expert/).
- Keep this January treaty account separate from subsequent diplomatic/legal developments.

topics.title: JNPA, container capacity and port logistics
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Port and unit
- **Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority**, **Nhava Sheva / Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra**, **west coast**; major container gateway. **TEU = twenty-foot equivalent unit**; a 40-foot container counts as two TEUs.
- **2024 throughput 7.05 million TEUs**, source **~11% growth**; target **10 million throughput by 2027**. Throughput is cargo actually handled; installed capacity is potential annual handling.
- Source capacity **7.6 → 10.4 million TEUs** is an expansion comparison; official **21 January 2025** release already describes **10+ million capacity**. Do not push that completed capacity milestone to 2027. [Ports Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2094901&lang=2&reg=48).
- “Largest” and **60% share** require denominator: **major ports** versus **all Indian ports**, and year. Do not assume JNPA exceeds every privately operated container port or handles 60% of all national cargo.
## Expansion and efficiency
- **Bharat Mumbai Container Terminal phase 2**, source **2.4 million TEU addition**; **Nhava Sheva Freeport Terminal upgrade**, nearly **₹2,000 crore projects** source aggregate.
- **Vadhavan**, separate deep-draft port development, not simply another berth inside Nhava Sheva.
- Solar-powered boat, indigenous **70-tonne bollard-pull tugs**, renewable power/electrification; tug rating is pulling force, not cargo capacity.
- Smart systems/automation, better turnaround, rail/road hinterland links and multimodal logistics can improve trade competitiveness and jobs.
- Constraints: project/clearance delays, coastal ecology/community concerns, financing and logistics bottlenecks. More terminal capacity alone does not guarantee lower transshipment dependence or actual cargo demand.

topics.title: Stray dogs: public safety and humane management
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 controversy
- Morocco to co-host **2030 FIFA World Cup with Spain/Portugal**; source discusses animal-welfare campaign allegations of culling **three million dogs**, **300,000 annually**, using poisoning/shooting.
- These are **reported allegations/estimates**, not independently verified official policy or completed numbers. Do not infer government intent from the article's speculation. Campaign evidence requires attribution: [OIPA January appeal](https://www.oipa.org/international/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2030-FIFA-World-Cup_OIPA-Appeal-January-2025.pdf).
## Ethical balance
- **Public health, rabies prevention and bite safety** alongside compassion, proportionality, ecological/public responsibility and accountable spending; urban appearance alone is a weak justification for cruelty.
- Humane population management: **sterilisation + vaccination**, responsible ownership, waste/food-source management, adoption where suitable and monitoring.
- India's **Animal Birth Control** framework is a comparison, not Moroccan law. Standards of **WOAH (formerly OIE)** do not automatically establish a particular international legal offence or give animals identical human constitutional rights.
- For a case study: verify allegations → assess risk → consult veterinary/public-health expertise → adopt lawful humane measures → publish outcomes and audit accountability.

topics.title: World Economic Forum and global indices
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution and Davos
- **1971, Klaus Schwab**: not-for-profit **European Management Forum**; renamed **World Economic Forum, 1987**. Headquarters **Cologny/Geneva, Switzerland**; offices New York, San Francisco, Beijing and Tokyo.
- Swiss recognition as an international organisation in **2015** does not make it a UN agency or a treaty-based global government. Dialogue among business, government, academia and civil society; stakeholder approach to economic/social challenges.
- Annual meeting **20–24 January 2025, Davos**; source about **3,000 participants**, members and selected invitees. Partner corporations largely fund activities; source describes roughly **1,000 leading member companies**, typically large-turnover enterprises, not a minimum turnover required of every attendee. [WEF history](https://www.weforum.org/stories/forum-institutional/world-economic-forum-davos-at-50-history-a-timeline-of-highlights/).
## Report recall
- **Global Gender Gap Report/Index; Global Risks Report; Global Competitiveness Report**; travel/tourism competitiveness/development reports.
- Source also lists **Global Information Technology Report** and **Global Enabling Trade Report**: historical report families; do not assume every title continues as an annual WEF publication with unchanged co-publishers.
- PYQ answers: **2017 Gender Gap ranking → WEF; 2009 founder → Klaus Schwab; 2019 Global Competitiveness Report → WEF**. Full questions in common prelims JSON.
- Report trap: **Human Development Report → UNDP**, not WEF. The weekly coaching test repeats WEF facts but is not a UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: Dark oxygen and polymetallic nodules
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Deep-sea finding
- **2024 study**, dark abyssal **Clarion–Clipperton Zone**, around **4,000 m** depth: oxygen increase recorded near **polymetallic nodules** without photosynthesis; January 2025 reports follow-up research plans.
- Nodules contain principally **manganese/iron** with valuable **nickel, cobalt and copper**; source also mentions lithium, which is not their principal commercial target.
- Proposed mechanism: electrochemical potentials across nodules may support **water splitting**. Observed oxygen production and the suggested **“geobattery” explanation** are distinct; electrolysis is not demonstrated as the sole settled mechanism.
- Photosynthesis by plants/algae/cyanobacteria is a major oxygen source, but “all oxygen can only be made by photosynthesis” is incorrect.
- Reproducibility, controls and ecological significance need study; deep-sea mining could disturb poorly understood seafloor processes/habitats. [Original research](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41561-024-01480-8).

topics.title: SCOT and space situational awareness
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 launch
- **SCOT = Space Camera for Object Tracking**, **Digantara**; commercial **space situational awareness (SSA)** satellite on **SpaceX Transporter-12**, **14 January**, Vandenberg, California; **sun-synchronous orbit**.
- Tracks **resident space objects** to support collision avoidance, safe operations and security. Developer's reported **5 cm** tracking capability needs observing conditions; no sensor provides unrestricted detection of every object at every instant.
- Space-based observation reduces terrestrial weather/geographic constraints but retains field-of-view, illumination, orbital geometry and processing limitations. Backers listed: **Aditya Birla Ventures, SIDBI**.
- Co-launches: **Pixxel's first three Firefly hyperspectral satellites**; Hyderabad **XDLINX Spacelabs' ELEVATION-1** for US **Almagest Space Corporation**.
- **SSA = know/track orbital environment; Earth observation = observe Earth's surface**. Different missions can share a launch.

topics.title: Goby fishes and Coringa mangroves
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Distribution records
- ZSI records **Hemigobius hoevenii** and **Mugilogobius tigrinus** in **Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary, Andhra Pradesh**, Godavari-estuary mangroves.
- Previously unrecorded in Andhra Pradesh; **M. tigrinus** reported first on India's **east coast**. **New locality records, not newly named species**.
- Source inventory: **135 coastal Indian goby species; 95 in Indian mangroves; 53 at Coringa**—study-specific counts.
## Ecology
- Usually small bottom-dwelling fishes; many marine/estuarine species, with freshwater forms too. Commonly fused pelvic fins form a weak suction disc; morphology/diet varies across species.
- Abundant in tropical, also temperate coasts/reefs/mangroves. Food-web roles, benthic ecology and potential environmental indicators; some island freshwater systems depend strongly on gobies.
- Protect estuarine water quality and mangrove habitat rather than equating a regional discovery with an automatic threatened-species category.
- Weekly practice Q23 prints an inconsistent code explanation; both stated locality records are correct in its account, not a new taxonomic discovery.

topics.title: Musi River and World Monuments Watch
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## River recall
- **Anantagiri Hills near Vicarabad, Telangana → Hyderabad → Krishna near Wazirabad, Nalgonda region**; Krishna tributary.
- **Osman Sagar** on Musi; **Himayat Sagar** on its tributary **Esi**. Do not place both dams on the same main channel.
- Esi/Musa headwater descriptions do not imply the whole river is only the source's **8 + 13 km**; Hyderabad's old/new city lie on opposite sides.
## 2025 Watch
- **Musi River Historic Buildings** and Gujarat's **Bhuj Historic Water Systems** included in **2025 World Monuments Watch**.
- **World Monuments Fund**, New York-based heritage organisation; Watch launched **1996**, biennial nomination/advocacy programme. **Not UNESCO World Heritage inscription**.
- Risks: climate/water stress, disasters, conflict and insensitive development/tourism. Heritage preservation should support living communities and resilient urban planning. [2025 WMF Watch](https://www.wmf.org/world-monuments-watch/2025).

topics.title: Sanchar Saathi and National Broadband Mission 2.0
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Citizen telecom protection
- **17 January 2025**, Department of Telecommunications: **Sanchar Saathi mobile app**; report suspected fraudulent communications through **Chakshu**, check connections in one's name, request blocking/tracing of lost/stolen mobiles, verify handset authenticity using **IMEI**.
- IMEI identifies a handset; blocking/tracing assistance does not guarantee recovery. Suspected-communication reporting differs from complaint/remedy for money already lost.
## NBM 2.0 targets: 2030
- Optical fibre connectivity to **2.70 lakh villages**; **95% uptime**; broadband access for **90% anchor institutions**, including schools, health centres, Anganwadis and Panchayat offices.
- Source Right of Way clearance goal **30 days**, from about **60 days**, alongside **Telecommunications Act 2023 / RoW Rules 2024**; approval-time targets are not achieved performance everywhere.
- **Government/PSU fibre mapping by 2026**, **PM Gati Shakti** coordination; **Call Before u Dig (CBuD)** reduces excavation damage through utility–excavator coordination.
- Infrastructure + affordable access + reliability + digital literacy/security determine meaningful inclusion. [Official launch](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2093732&lang=2&reg=3).

topics.title: National Turmeric Board and value chains
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- Constituted **October 2023**; launched **14 January 2025**, **Nizamabad, Telangana**; **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, chairman **Palle Ganga Reddy**.
- Representation: Commerce, AYUSH, Pharmaceuticals, Agriculture, research bodies, farmers/exporters and rotating State representatives; source launch States **Maharashtra, Telangana, Meghalaya**.
- Research, higher yield/quality, processing/value addition, logistics, export standards and markets; promote credible evidence for traditional/medicinal uses, not claims turmeric cures every disease.
## Production and trade
- India: leading producer/consumer/exporter, **30+ varieties**, source **over 70% of world production**. Leading States include **Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu**; destinations **Bangladesh, UAE, USA, Malaysia**.
- Official **2023–24** cultivation **3.05 lakh ha**, production **10.74 lakh tonnes**; retain crop-year labels. [Commerce Ministry launch](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2092719&lang=2&reg=48).
- Better planting material + extension + processing/quality assurance + diversified markets can improve producer income. Volume growth alone does not guarantee remunerative farm prices.

topics.title: Sada lateritic plateaus and seasonal ecology
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Konkan landscape
- **Sada**: local term for lateritic rock plateaus in **Konkan**, also called **pathar**; weathered ferruginous surfaces, seasonal herbaceous vegetation and pools. Compare **Kaas plateau, Satara**, without equating every Sada with Kaas.
- Monsoon biodiversity and dry-season bare appearance: **seasonal habitat ≠ wasteland**. Fractures/pools support infiltration, runoff regulation and groundwater recharge.
- Source regional survey records **459 plant species, 105 Konkan endemics; 31 reptiles, 13 amphibians, 169 birds, 41 mammals**. Not a census of every individual plateau.
- Rock engravings/geoglyphs testify to prehistoric activity; source **around 10,000 years BP** is approximate and not a securely established date for every engraving.
## Threats and protection
- Orchards/cultivation, construction and land-cover conversion; missing habitat recognition can hide losses.
- Map seasonal ecology, protect drainage/microhabitats and heritage, regulate conversion and involve local communities. Small barren-looking areas can carry high endemism.
- Embedded geomorphology PYQ graphic supplies partial questions only; full originals are pending review, and its **CDS 2014** item is not a CSE question.

topics.title: Chronic wasting disease and prions
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Cervid disease
- **CWD**, fatal neurodegenerative disease of **deer, elk, moose and related cervids**; caused by **prions, misfolded infectious proteins**, not bacteria/viruses.
- Abnormal protein promotes further misfolding → brain damage/spongiform changes. Spread through secretions/excretions and contaminated environments; prions may persist in soil/water.
- Long incubation, source **18–24 months**; weight loss, abnormal behaviour/movement, salivation and excessive thirst/urination. Visible signs may lag infection.
- No established cure/vaccine in the January account. **No confirmed human infection**; potential cross-species risk needs surveillance, not a claim proven to infect humans. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/chronic-wasting/about/index.html).
- “Zombie deer” is a media nickname. Prion disease differs from Huntington's inherited HTT disorder.

topics.title: Bhargavastra and counter-drone systems
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 test account
- **Economic Explosives Limited, Solar Industries**: **Bhargavastra** counter-drone system using guided micro-missiles; source detection **about 6 km**, engagement **over 2.5 km**, salvo capability **about 64**. These are reported configuration/test figures, not guaranteed in all terrain/conditions.
- Mobile deployment, radar/sensors and command/fire-control integration; protect bases/assets from small drones and coordinated attacks.
| Approach | Mechanism / limitation |
| --- | --- |
| **Soft kill** | Jam/spoof communications or navigation; resistant/autonomous drones may bypass it |
| **Hard kill** | Physical interception, guns/missiles/energy systems; debris and cost matter |
## Swarms
- Multiple drones coordinate tasks through centralised/distributed or pre-programmed control. **SWARM is not a universal expansion of “Smart War-Fighting Array…”**, and there is no universal rule that a swarm must contain at least three vehicles.
- Reconnaissance/strike, search/rescue, firefighting and mapping potential; coordination, spectrum, autonomy and identification of friendly drones matter.
- Keep January micro-missile reporting separate from later variants/test announcements.

topics.title: Funnel-web spiders: taxonomic revision
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 revision
- Former Sydney funnel-web grouping resolved into **Atrax robustus**, **A. montanus** and newly named **A. christenseni**—**Newcastle funnel-web, “Big Boy”**, named for **Kane Christensen**.
- Newcastle region, eastern Australia; notably large males/fangs/venom glands. Source **9 cm** figure is not established as body length; size does not alone prove universally greater venom potency.
- Dark, burrowing spiders in moist/shaded forest and suburban habitats; funnel-shaped webs and prominent spinnerets.
- Venom affects nerve signalling; medically important bites, especially some males. **Antivenom introduced 1981**, with no recorded Australian funnel-web deaths since introduction in the museum account. [Australian Museum revision](https://australian.museum/about/organisation/media-centre/sydney-funnel-web-spider-reclassified/).
- Source **36 species in Atrax/Hadronyche/Illawarra** reflects an older count; do not retain it as an updated post-revision total. Not Australia's largest spider merely because a large funnel-web was identified.

topics.title: Atomic Energy Commission and DAE
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Institutional timeline
- **AEC first constituted August 1948** under Department of Scientific Research; **DAE established 3 August 1954**, directly under **Prime Minister**.
- Commission reconstituted **1 March 1958** within DAE; **1958 is not its original creation**. DAE Secretary is ex-officio AEC chairman; appointments follow the government resolution. Headquarters **Mumbai**. [DAE institutional history](https://dae.gov.in/atomic-energy-commission/).
## Functions
- Atomic-energy policy and coordination; nuclear-power programmes, fuel-cycle capability and research.
- Uranium/fuel fabrication, heavy water, reactors, reprocessing and radioactive-waste management; resource development and research into fast reactors/fusion.
- Accelerators, lasers, materials and biological research; radioisotopes/radiation for **medicine, agriculture, food preservation and industry**.
- **AEC policy body ≠ AERB safety regulator**; DAE non-power applications should not be confused with only electricity generation.

topics.title: Kokborok language and script debate
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Tripura
- Language of **Borok/Tripuri communities**, **Sino-Tibetan family**; **kok = speech/language, borok = people**. Recognised as an official language of Tripura **19 January 1979**, observed as Kokborok Day.
- **2011 Census** source: **880,537 speakers**, about **23.97%** of Tripura population; not a 2025 census count.
- Debate over **Roman versus Bengali script**; student organisations including TSF/NESO seek script choices for education/examinations. Script preference differs from linguistic family or official-language status.
- Source mentions early grammars by **Daulat Ahmed (Kokboroma, 1897/98)** and **Thakur Radhamohan Debbarma (1900)**. Its alleged **first-century Raj Ratnakar** is not a verified surviving first-century linguistic attestation.
- Language preservation: teaching material, trained teachers, consistent exam access, community participation and digital resources.

topics.title: Mud volcanoes and temporary islands
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism
- Pressurised **gas, water and sediment** escape through weak rocks → mud eruptions/cones. Often sedimentary/oil-field settings; **methane/hydrocarbons**, not necessarily magma.
- Repeated eruption builds cones, erosion removes them; size/hazard varies. **Geothermal mud pots** involving boiling water/altered rock are a related-looking but distinct process, not a complete explanation for every sedimentary mud volcano.
- Source “only warm mud / always less hazardous” is unsafe generalisation: large flows can bury infrastructure, and flammable gas may ignite/explode.
## Kumani Bank
- **Caspian Sea, off Azerbaijan**: eruption formed island early **2023**, nearly eroded away by **December 2024**; satellite comparison reported **January 2025**. [NASA images](https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/satellites-spot-a-ghost-island-153799/).
- Other reported regions: **Ukraine, Italy, Romania, Iran, Pakistan, Indonesia, China; Alaska, California, Trinidad, Venezuela, Colombia**.
- Source **~1,000 on land/shallow water** is an inventory estimate, not exhaustive global/submarine total. **Mud eruption ≠ lava eruption**; isolated small cones do not establish every system is small.

topics.title: Bharat Ranbhoomi Darshan and border tourism
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Army Day initiative
- **15 January 2025** launch: Army/Defence Ministry with Tourism Ministry and civil authorities; app/website with historical accounts, virtual visits and **permit/travel information**, linked to **Incredible India**.
- Source gives **75 sites** and elsewhere “75 other sites”; treat as reported coverage, not an exact reconciled inventory. **Galwan, Ladakh; Nathu La/Cho La, Sikkim; Longewala, Thar Desert**, and other border locations.
- **Doklam** is a disputed Bhutan–China plateau near the India–Bhutan–China junction; do not treat it as an undisputed Indian battlefield with unrestricted entry.
- Recall **1962 war; 1967 Nathu La/Cho La clashes; 1971 Longewala**. Source practice answer excluding **Siachen** is misleading: official site list includes **Siachen Base Camp**. [Ministry's site list](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2099162&lang=2&reg=48).
- Border livelihoods/connectivity and public understanding of military history; permits, operational readiness, ecology, local consultation and visitor safety constrain access. App launch does not remove all border restrictions.

topics.title: Huntington disease and inherited neurodegeneration
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Genetic mechanism
- **HTT gene CAG-repeat expansion** → abnormal **huntingtin** protein → progressive neuronal dysfunction/loss, particularly **basal ganglia and cortex**.
- **Autosomal dominant**; affected heterozygous parent gives each child a **50% inheritance risk**. Not contagious and not a prion infection.
- **Chorea**, abnormal posture/movements, cognitive decline and behavioural/emotional changes; unusual eye movements/tremors may occur.
- Source **3–7 per 100,000**, more common in European ancestry; prevalence varies. Often **15–20 years survival after onset** is an average, not an individual prediction.
- No cure reversing the disease in the January account; specialist medicines and supportive care manage symptoms, with genetic counselling where appropriate. [NIH clinical genetics](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1305/).

topics.title: Indian grey wolf and Bankapur sanctuary
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Habitat and news
- January report: **eight pups at Bankapur Wolf Sanctuary, Koppal, Karnataka**, State's first dedicated wolf sanctuary.
- Source calls it India's second after **Mahuadanr, established 1976**, now **Jharkhand**, not present-day Bihar.
- Traditional subspecies name **Canis lupus pallipes**; Indian wolf lineages/taxonomic assessments need care. Smaller packs, relatively less vocal, thin coat suited to warm **grassland, scrub and semi-arid pastoral landscapes**; often nocturnal/crepuscular.
- Source's broad Israel–subcontinent distribution is a traditional subspecies range, not proof all populations are one uniform Indian genetic lineage.
## Conservation traps
- Source **IUCN Least Concern** refers to the broad **grey-wolf assessment**, not proof Indian populations are secure or a current independent Indian-wolf assessment.
- **Wildlife (Protection) Act Schedule I**; **CITES Appendix I** includes relevant Indian wolf population listing, not every grey-wolf population worldwide.
- Habitat loss/fragmentation, prey depletion and persecution; protect open habitats as well as forest reserves. Bankapur scrub, hills/caves also support blackbuck, foxes, hares, porcupines, leopards and peafowl.

topics.title: Pralay missile and DRDO Republic Day display
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Tactical strike
- **DRDO Pralay**, mobile-launch **solid-propellant surface-to-surface tactical ballistic missile**, **150–500 km**; advanced navigation/guidance and manoeuvrability for battlefield targets such as command centres, radar and airbases.
- **Conventional strike role**. Source **350–700 kg** is a reported payload range; its claim of nuclear warheads/strengthening nuclear second-strike capability is unsupported. **Tactical strike ≠ nuclear second strike**.
- Maiden test **22 December 2021**, **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha**. Embedded “two-stage Mach 1.6” schematic is not an authoritative specification; do not memorise it as verified missile performance. [Official test](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1784136&lang=2&reg=48&s=09).
## Republic Day 2025 planned display
- DRDO theme **Raksha Kavach: multilayer protection against multi-domain threats**; **laser-based directed energy weapon**, Pralay and integrated protection.
- Tableau systems: **QRSAM; Arudhra medium-power radar; drone detection/deterrence/destruction; ATAGS 155 mm/52 calibre; indigenous unmanned aerial system**.
- **2024 milestones**: long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile, **Zorawar light tank, ABHED lightweight bulletproof jacket**. Other contingents: **Nag, Pinaka, BrahMos, Akash**.
- Display/test achievement differs from universal operational deployment. [DRDO announcement](https://drdo.gov.in/drdo/en/documents/press-release/theme-raksha-kavach-multilayer-protection-against-multi-domain-threats-drdo).

topics.title: WHO, US withdrawal and global health governance
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 development
- **20 January 2025**, newly inaugurated President **Donald Trump** initiated US withdrawal; he was not a former president acting outside office. WHO's **21 January** statement sought reconsideration. **Announcement of intent ≠ completed withdrawal that day**. [WHO statement](https://www.who.int/news/item/21-01-2025-who-comments-on-united-states--announcement-of-intent-to-withdraw).
- Source **~18% US funding** is a dated donor-share comparison, not a permanent fraction of every biennial budget. Assessed contributions and voluntary, often earmarked funds differ.
## Why it matters
- Financing/service disruptions for HIV, TB, malaria and lower-income health systems; surveillance, outbreak data and coordinated response weaken when major partners disengage.
- Pathogens cross borders; domestic health security depends on international cooperation. Withdrawal reduces influence over reform and may increase fragmentation.
- Alleged political bias/inefficiency should be assessed with evidence. Editorial advocates reform: transparent decisions, faster operations and **predictable less-earmarked finance**, reducing donor dependence.
- Mains balance: national sovereignty/accountability concerns versus global public goods, equitable access and collective health security.

topics.title: Tuberculosis: elimination and health-system gaps
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease and resistance
- **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, chiefly airborne from infectious pulmonary TB; lungs commonly affected, but **extrapulmonary TB (EP-TB)** involves other organs. **Latent infection is not contagious active disease**.
- Symptoms: persistent cough/sputum, weight/appetite loss, fever/night sweats and fatigue. Risks include **undernutrition, HIV, diabetes, smoking/alcohol**, and occupational exposure/social barriers.
- **MDR-TB**: resistance to at least **isoniazid + rifampicin**. **Pre-XDR**: MDR/rifampicin-resistant TB plus any fluoroquinolone resistance. **XDR** adds resistance to **bedaquiline or linezolid**. Source graphic's “isoniazid, rifampicin, fluoroquinolone and second-line injectable” reflects the **old definition**. [WHO 2021 update](https://www.who.int/news/item/27-01-2021-who-announces-updated-definitions-of-extensively-drug-resistant-tuberculosis).
- **BPaLM = bedaquiline + pretomanid + linezolid + moxifloxacin**; shorter regimen for eligible drug-resistant cases under clinical/programme criteria. Other named drugs **isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol, streptomycin** are not an instruction to self-combine treatment.
## Dated targets and burden
- India **2025 elimination ambition**, global **2030 End TB/SDG horizon**; ambition is not proof disease eradicated. **NTEP**, **Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan/Ni-kshay Mitras**, nutrition/community support and preventive therapy for eligible high-risk contacts; source **Project Akshaya Plus** contact-tracing/testing example.
- Source report **~26% global burden**, **EP-TB 24% notified cases**, **>95% treatment initiation**, **24% mortality reduction from 2015**: retain indicator/period labels; initiating notified cases differs from treatment coverage among all estimated incident cases.
- Graphic world deaths **1.32 million (2022) → 1.25 million (2023)**, about **3,500 daily**; low/middle-income countries **87% burden**, Indonesia/China/Philippines/Pakistan plus India account for a major share. Notifications reflect diagnosis/reporting, not automatic incidence increase.
## Gaps and response
- Drug/diagnostic supply interruptions, including source **2023 shortages**; delayed EP-TB diagnosis, cartridge/staff shortages and underused **CBNAAT/Truenat**; high costs and migrant/occupational barriers.
- Decentralised rapid molecular testing and referral, trained workers, uninterrupted procurement, adherence/nutrition support and portable migrant records.
- **Idukki–Kudumbashree SHGs**: community participation; **Vietnam active case finding** in high-risk groups: adapt rather than copy uncritically.
- Prevention → find cases early → test resistance → complete appropriate treatment → support contacts/nutrition → monitor outcomes. COVID disruption and social determinants require sustained action beyond targets.

topics.title: INS Sarvekshak and hydrographic diplomacy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Mauritius survey: January 2025
- **INS Sarvekshak**, Indian Navy **Darshak-class hydrographic survey vessel**, Southern Naval Command, **Kochi**; completed Mauritius survey covering **over 25,000 square nautical miles**. Survey fair sheet and charts handed over; maritime navigation, port planning and resource governance benefits.
- **SAGAR = Security and Growth for All in the Region**; cooperation builds partner capacity and maritime trust. Source five-year regional record **89,000 sq km / 96 charts** uses a different unit from the Mauritius survey. [Navy release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2095401&lang=2&reg=48).
- Multi-beam echo sounder, side-scan sonar and digital processing; integral **Chetak helicopter**. Source complement **15 officers/175 sailors** is a vessel description, not a universal survey staffing norm.
- Other cooperation: **Sri Lanka, Seychelles, Tanzania, Kenya** and earlier Mauritius missions.
## Hydrography versus oceanography
- Measures/describes **physical water-body features**, depth/seabed, tides/currents and navigational shoreline aids; forecasts relevant changes and supports safe navigation.
- Ships/boats use sonar/echo sounding; aircraft **laser bathymetry** and satellites contribute where suitable.
- Oceanography studies wider marine processes; hydrography's charting/navigational purpose is a distinction, not exclusion of overlapping science.

topics.title: Rhodamine B and food adulteration
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Industrial dye ≠ food colour
- Water-soluble **fluorescent red/pink dye**, used in textiles, paper, leather/paints and laboratories. Source green-powder description is not a dependable identification test for every formulation.
- **Not a permitted food colour in India**; adulterated cotton candy and other foods illustrate enforcement concern. Applicable law: **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**, with food-additive regulations; penalties depend on offence and harm, not one universal sentence.
- Toxicological concerns include oxidative/cellular injury and possible organ/neurotoxicity/carcinogenicity; animal/laboratory hazard evidence does not establish every exposure causes human cancer.
- Source blanket “banned worldwide / global consensus” is not a verified survey of all countries' law. **Bright colour alone cannot identify the chemical**; laboratory testing and enforcement are necessary.
- Licensing, supply-chain checks, approved additives, targeted inspection/testing and public awareness; avoid equating an industrial dye with a safe edible additive.

topics.title: Lake Naivasha and invasive water hyacinth
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Location and livelihoods
- **Kenya, southern Rift Valley**, shallow **freshwater lake**, surrounded by volcanic terrain; rivers **Malewa and Gilgil**, draining central Kenyan highlands/Aberdare region.
- **Ramsar site**; papyrus (**Cyperus papyrus**), submerged **Potamogeton**, waterbirds and mammals. Supports **floriculture, fishing** and nearby **geothermal power** activity. [Ramsar record](https://rsis.ramsar.org/ris/724).
## Water hyacinth
- South American invasive floating plant, **Eichhornia crassipes** (also classified as **Pontederia crassipes**); source introduction to Kenya in **1980s** is a regional historical account.
- Nutrient enrichment supports rapid growth → dense mats shade submerged vegetation and impede surface gas exchange/navigation → oxygen/habitat and fishing problems. “Thrives in contamination” does not mean every contaminant promotes growth.
- Control nutrient inputs, monitor infestation and combine suitable mechanical/biological management with safe disposal; indiscriminate herbicide use can harm lake ecology.
- Practice's black-rhinoceros distractor does not establish absence of every rhino from the wider landscape; lake identity rests on location, hydrology and wetland ecology.

topics.title: Great Barrier Reef and coral bleaching
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Map and conservation
- World's largest **coral reef system**, **Coral Sea, northeast Australia/Queensland**, Pacific; roughly **2,300 km**, **~3,000 reefs**. Marine Park **344,400 sq km**; source rounded **350,000** and World Heritage area measurements use differing boundaries. **Not every square kilometre is living coral**. [Reef Authority facts](https://www.gbrmpa.gov.au/learn/fascinating-facts-about-great-barrier-reef).
- **UNESCO World Heritage, 1981**, managed largely by **Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority/Reef Authority**. Source around **400 coral types, 1,500 fishes, 4,000 molluscs**; dugongs and green turtles are notable fauna. Source **10% global coral ecosystems** needs denominator/date.
- Platform/patch reefs, elongated reefs/walls and **fringing reefs**; classic evolution **fringing → barrier → atoll** with subsidence and continued growth, not a universal history for every reef.
## Coral recall
- **Coral polyps are animals**, commonly colonial; reef-building **hard corals deposit calcium carbonate**, unlike soft corals' usual structure. Many tropical corals associate with **zooxanthellae**.
- Heat/other stress → loss of symbiotic algae/pigment → **bleaching**. Bleached coral is **not necessarily dead**, but prolonged stress causes starvation/disease and mortality.
- Threats: warming, acidification, sediment/pollution, salinity changes, destructive fishing/coastal development and tourism pressure; protect water quality and habitats alongside emissions reduction.
- Benefits: biodiversity, coast protection, fisheries/jobs/tourism and research. Global reef biodiversity claims concern all coral reefs, not GBR alone.
- Indian examples: **Gulf of Kachchh, Gulf of Mannar, Andaman–Nicobar, Lakshadweep**; source also mentions Malvan. Conservation examples: **International Coral Reef Initiative**, **Global Coral Reef R&D Accelerator Platform**, India's **National Coastal Mission**; cryopreservation/larval restoration and mineral-accretion **Biorock** are tools, not substitutes for controlling stress.

topics.title: Culicoides midges and bluetongue disease
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Andaman–Nicobar survey
- ZSI survey **2022–23**, reported January 2025: **23 Culicoides species**, **13 first Indian records**; Indian inventory **93 valid species** in this account. New national records do not mean 13 species newly described to science.
- **Culicoides**, family **Ceratopogonidae**, order **Diptera**, tiny biting midges (“bhusi flies”). **Not all insects called midges belong to this genus or bite**; non-biting chironomid graphics are a different family.
- First records listed: **C. barnetti, gouldi, flaviscutellaris, flavipunctatus, hui, histrio, guttifer, perornatus, okinawensis, quatei, obscurus, coronalis, kusaiensis**.
- Cosmopolitan genus, source excludes **New Zealand/Antarctica**. Females of blood-feeding species bite livestock/wildlife; sexes/species also differ in nectar use. “Exclusively blood, never nectar” is misleading.
## One Health
- Source **17/23 known human-biters**, five bluetongue-vector species; no human disease transmission documented **in this survey**, not proof all midges globally lack human-health effects.
- **Bluetongue**, viral ruminant disease; fever, swelling, salivation and sometimes bluish tongue; sheep can suffer severe/fatal disease. Vector competence differs among species.
- Source family-level counts **~60 viruses / 40 protozoans / 24 filarial nematodes** are reported pathogen associations, not proof each surveyed species transmits every one.
- Identify species, monitor vectors/livestock, reduce suitable breeding exposure and coordinate animal-health surveillance.

topics.title: Kalaripayattu and Indian martial arts
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Kerala tradition
- **Kalari**: training ground/gymnasium; **payattu**: martial practice. Integrates physical conditioning, armed/unarmed combat and mind–body coordination; one of India's longstanding martial traditions.
| Training stage | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| **Maippayattu** | Body conditioning |
| **Kolthari** | Wooden weapons: sticks/staves |
| **Angathari** | Metal weapons |
| **Verumkai** | Bare-hand fighting; anatomical knowledge |
- Northern/Malabar styles named: **Vattenthirippu, Arappukkai, Pillathangi**.
- **Parasurama origin story is tradition**, not verified historical founding. Bodhidharma/Shaolin transmission narrative is disputed; source **fifth-century / Thanjavur once part of Kerala** claim should not be learnt as settled history.
- January controversy: role in **38th National Games, Uttarakhand**, beginning **28 January 2025**; demonstration status and competitive-medal inclusion are distinct.
## Regional martial-art map
- **Huyen Langlon/Thang-ta, Manipur**: sword/spear armed practice and **Sarit Sarak** unarmed combat.
- **Lathi Khela, Bengal**: staff; **Gatka, Punjab**: Sikh martial practice with sticks/swords, linked to **Guru Hargobind** and later Sikh tradition; source federation **2018** is an organisational date, not origin of the art.
- **Silambam, Tamil Nadu**: staff/other weapons, Tamil diaspora including Malaysia; deity/sage origin accounts are traditional.
- **Kathi Samu, Andhra Pradesh**: sword practice in **garidi**, stick practice as preparation; **Paika Akhada, Odisha**: warrior training with rhythmic performance/drums.
- **Pari Khanda, Bihar/eastern tradition**: sword–shield; links to Chhau practice do not make every local martial form separately UNESCO-listed.
- **Thoda, Himachal Pradesh**: archery-based sport/performance, Baisakhi and Mahabharata-themed groups; **Mallakhamb, Maharashtra/Madhya Pradesh**: gymnastic pole/rope practice, malla = wrestler, khamb = pole.
- **Kalaripayattu, Mallakhamb, Gatka, Thang-ta** inducted into Khelo India Youth Games programme in the source's historical account; not proof all described arts are medal events in every competition.

topics.title: National Board for Wildlife and statutory safeguards
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Legal identity
- **Section 5A, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972**, introduced by **Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act 2002**, **Act 16 of 2003**. Source **2022 creation** is wrong; predecessor **Indian Board for Wildlife, 1952**.
- **Prime Minister chair; Environment Minister vice-chair**, senior government representatives, institutions, NGOs, nominated conservationists/ecologists and rotating State/UT representatives. Source **47 members** is a reported composition count, not the safest substitute for statutory categories.
- Member-secretary: **Additional Director General of Forests (Wildlife)/Director of Wildlife Preservation**.
- **Section 5B Standing Committee**: vice-chairperson, member-secretary **plus no more than ten nominated Board members**; not “ten total” and not an independent external regulator. [Amendment text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/6199/1/wild_act_2002.pdf).
## Roles and limits
- Advises on policy, conservation and protected-area assessment; Standing Committee exercises delegated functions/project scrutiny.
- Statutory safeguards cover protected-area habitat diversion/destruction, relevant tourism development and boundary changes; tiger-reserve denotification requires **NTCA recommendation + NBWL approval**, with applicable State/central procedures.
- NBWL recommendation **does not replace every forest/environment clearance** or permit all activity automatically. Applicable protection differs by sanctuary, national park, tiger reserve and eco-sensitive area.
- January report: refusal of **soapstone mining proposal near Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary, Uttarakhand**; compare mineral extraction, habitat/hydrology and site-specific legal constraints.

topics.title: NASAMS and networked air defence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System
- **National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System**, **Kongsberg (Norway) + Raytheon (USA)**; ground-based short/medium-range **networked air defence**, fielded by Norway **1994**.
- Radar/sensors → **Fire Distribution Centre** → distributed launchers; **AIM-120 AMRAAM** adapted for ground launch, with configuration-dependent other missiles. Aircraft, helicopters, cruise missiles and drones are typical targets.
- Modular open architecture, active radar and passive electro-optical/IR inputs; distributed components improve survivability/interoperability, not immunity to jamming.
- Source **75 km radar / 30 km engagement**, **six missiles per launcher**, **three launchers / 72 targets** combine configuration-specific claims. **Detection range ≠ missile range; launcher inventory ≠ simultaneous target capacity**. [Manufacturer description](https://www.kongsberg.com/what-we-do/defence-and-security/integrated-air-and-missile-defence/nasams-air-defence-system/).
## January context
- Taiwan reported planned **north/Taipei deployment** of purchased systems; procurement, delivery and deployment dates differ.
- Users source lists Norway, Spain, US, Finland, Hungary, Netherlands, Australia, Indonesia, Qatar, Oman and Lithuania; **13-country count** is dated/incomplete, not a permanent membership list. US capital-region protection since **2005**.
- Practice's “Canada never uses NASAMS” distractor requires date/end-user distinction; Canada's procurement for Ukraine differs from Canadian domestic operational deployment. Do not memorise a timeless negative.

topics.title: Oyster proteins and antimicrobial resistance research
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## January research finding
- **Southern Cross University**, oyster **haemolymph** proteins: laboratory antibacterial activity and improved action of conventional antibiotics against selected bacteria.
- **Antimicrobial proteins/peptides** are innate defences against microbes in marine habitats; potential drug leads require isolation, mechanism, toxicity, dosage and clinical validation. **Not an approved human treatment or evidence eating oysters cures resistant infection**. [University's 21 January account](https://www.scu.edu.au/news/2025/video---oyster-blood-proteins/).
## Biology traps
- **Mollusca → Bivalvia**; two irregular calcified shell valves, marine/brackish filter feeders drawing algae/particles across gills.
- Filtration depends on size, species and conditions; source **1.3 gallons/hour** is not a universal fixed rate. Many reproduce by broadcast spawning, with sex change in some species.
- Oysters have **nervous ganglia**, despite lacking a vertebrate-like brain/spinal cord. That alone does not establish a definitive capacity/absence of pain.
- Source **eyes all over body** confuses oysters with eye-bearing bivalves such as scallops; shell closure/sensory response does not require that anatomy.
- University describes **Sydney rock oyster** proteins disrupting/preventing bacterial **biofilms**, one reason for improved antibiotic action in laboratory work.

topics.title: Mount McKinley–Denali and Alaska geology
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 naming context
- **20 January US executive direction** to restore **Mount McKinley** name for **Denali**, **North America's highest peak**, **Alaska Range, south-central Alaska**. Mountain renaming differs from renaming **Denali National Park and Preserve**.
- Two summits, higher southern summit; mainly granitic massif with tectonic uplift/erosion. Not a volcano and not on the US–Canada boundary.
- Source uplift history **about 60 million years** describes long tectonic history, not instantaneous formation of the present summit.
- Large vertical relief above surroundings, source **~5,500 m**; **relief is not summit elevation above sea level**. Snow/ice feed **Kahiltna, Muldrow, Peters, Ruth, Traleika** glaciers.
## Denali Fault
- Major **strike-slip fault system**; long-term horizontal movement rearranges geological units. Source study correlates three formerly connected **terminal-suture-zone** sites and estimates **~483 km displacement over millions of years**, not one earthquake or annual movement.
- **Suture**: zone of past terrane/plate joining; later strike-slip offsets can separate once-contiguous features. Map locations and differentiate vertical mountain uplift from lateral fault displacement.

topics.title: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis after tuberculosis
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease distinction
- **CPA**, chronic lung disease caused by **Aspergillus**, often **A. fumigatus**, an environmental mould in soil/dust/decaying vegetation; spores inhaled, not ordinarily person-to-person transmission.
- **Pre-existing lung cavities/damage**, especially post-TB, COPD or sarcoidosis, predispose. Severe immunosuppression is particularly important for **invasive aspergillosis**; CPA can occur without it. Do not collapse all Aspergillus syndromes into one.
- Persistent **three-month-plus respiratory symptoms**, cough/haemoptysis, weight loss, fatigue/breathlessness; fungal ball **aspergilloma** or chronic cavitary changes. **Post-TB symptoms ≠ automatically recurrent bacterial TB**.
- Diagnosis combines imaging and **Aspergillus IgG/other microbiology** with clinical context; antibody positivity alone is not the same as confirmed CPA. [CDC overview](https://www.cdc.gov/aspergillosis/about/index.html).
## Assam study
- January **2025**, Dibrugarh tea-community study: **128 tea gardens screened**, selected symptomatic sample **177**; clipping **17.8% CPA**, **18.5% among TB patients**, **48.9% among those who completed TB treatment**. These are study/subgroup estimates, not Assam-wide population percentages. [Original research](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pntd.0012756).
- Poverty, nutrition, occupational exposure and diagnostic access compound vulnerability. Clipping cites Assam TB **217 per lakh**, national prevalence survey **2019–21**, and CPA **60 per lakh** estimate; keep disease/period/estimate distinct.
- Source **1.2 million globally annually** is not an adequately defined current all-CPA incidence estimate; post-TB estimates and total disease prevalence must not be conflated.
## Care and policy
- Specialist **antifungals** such as itraconazole/voriconazole, selected surgery for serious fungal-ball bleeding and nutritional/underlying-disease support; treatment depends on form, resistance and patient assessment.
- Follow up TB survivors, train clinicians, improve affordable imaging/serology and antifungal access; better nutrition/living conditions support health, but ventilation alone cannot remove ubiquitous mould exposure.

topics.title: SANJAY battlefield surveillance system
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 flag-off
- **24 January**, **Indian Army + Bharat Electronics Limited**, indigenous automated **Battlefield Surveillance System (BSS)**, **Buy (Indian)**; **₹2,402 crore**.
- Planned phased induction into **brigades, divisions, corps**, **March–October 2025** in three phases. Flag-off and a planned induction schedule do not prove all units were deployed in January. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2095712&lang=2&reg=48).
## Data to decisions
- Ground/aerial sensor inputs → integration and removal of duplicate observations → **Common Surveillance Picture** → secure Army data/satellite networks → commander assessment.
- Improved border/intrusion awareness, network-centric coordination and decision speed in conventional/sub-conventional operations; technology absorption/domestic industry benefits.
- Surveillance system **does not itself guarantee correct identification or replace command responsibility**. Sensor quality, interoperability, resilient communications, cybersecurity and operator training determine performance.

topics.title: Indo-Pacific: geography, interests and cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Concept and map
- Connects **Indian and Pacific Ocean** strategic/economic systems; boundaries differ by country. India's broad vision extends from **African shores to the Americas**, rather than one universally fixed treaty region.
- **Hormuz**, Persian Gulf approach; **Malacca**, Indian Ocean–South China Sea route; sea lanes carry energy/trade. **South China Sea is a sea, not a strait/chokepoint**.
- Source **60% maritime trade / 60% GDP / two-thirds growth** are broad region/period-dependent estimates, not comparable exact annual shares without definitions.
## Issues
- US–China competition, Chinese maritime claims/artificial-island activity and BRI influence; diverse countries' interests cannot be reduced to identical blocs.
- South China Sea claims involve **China, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei**, with **Taiwan** also relevant; East China Sea **Senkaku/Diaoyu** dispute. Maritime rights/navigation governed by applicable international law, not merely influence over trade routes.
- Piracy, illegal fishing, arms/drug trafficking; climate hazards, sea-level rise, coral loss and marine pollution; militarisation and unequal infrastructure/capacity.
## India and regional mechanisms
- **Act East, ASEAN centrality, free/open/inclusive cooperation**, strategic autonomy and international law; security alongside connectivity, blue economy and disaster resilience. [India's 2018 policy address](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=179711).
| Mechanism | Distinction |
| --- | --- |
| **Quad** | India, USA, Japan, Australia; partnership, not a formal defence alliance |
| **AUKUS** | Australia, UK, USA; India is not a member |
| **IPEF** | Economic cooperation framework, not identical to a free-trade agreement |
| **IONS / Malabar** | Maritime dialogue / naval exercise, respectively |
- **Andaman–Nicobar Command**, naval capacity, partner exercises; island partnerships **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Seychelles**. **Sagarmala** domestic port-led development; **Chabahar** Iran connectivity project—different functions/locations.
- Balance partnerships, protect commerce and support smaller States' choices; technology/finance/infrastructure, readiness and environmental cooperation matter as much as declarations.

topics.title: Guillain–Barré syndrome and post-infection nerve injury
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and symptoms
- Rare **immune-mediated peripheral nerve disorder**: immune attack damages myelin and/or nerve fibres → weakness, tingling/numbness, reduced reflexes and sometimes paralysis.
- **Not contagious**; an antecedent infection may be transmissible. **Peripheral nervous system ≠ brain/spinal cord**. All ages affected, more often adults/men; background incidence roughly **1–2 per 100,000/year**, population-dependent.
- Common progression: legs → arms/face, impaired walking/coordination; swallowing/respiratory muscles may be affected. **Autonomic dysfunction** can disturb heart rate/blood pressure; weakness need not remain mild/temporary.
## Triggers and Pune context
- Often follows gastrointestinal/respiratory infection, notably **Campylobacter jejuni**, and **EBV/CMV**, among others. **Mycoplasma pneumoniae** is another recognised association; not every urinary infection causes GBS.
- Surgery and rare associations with particular vaccines occur; **infections carry greater GBS risk than their relevant preventive vaccines**. Source's broad “trauma/stress” list is not evidence ordinary emotional stress is an established routine cause.
- **January 2025 Pune cluster**, central/State teams investigating; clipping reports **73 cases / 14 ventilated as of 25 January**, a dated snapshot, not final outbreak totals or proof a specific water source caused every case.
## Treatment and recovery
- **IVIG**, pooled donor immunoglobulins, or **plasma exchange** can modify the immune attack; respiratory/cardiac monitoring, supportive care and rehabilitation matter.
- Antivirals are not the main treatment for the immune disorder; management of an identified antecedent infection is a separate decision.
- Many recover over weeks/months, sometimes much longer, with persistent disability in some; no instant curative treatment. Rapidly progressive weakness/breathing difficulty requires urgent clinical assessment. [WHO explanation](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/guillain-barr%C3%A9-syndrome).

topics.title: Dhanauri wetland and Sarus crane conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Location and notification
- **Dhanauri, near Dankaur/Greater Noida**, **Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh**, near Jewar airport; wider **Yamuna floodplain/basin**, source about **15 km from Yamuna**, with Okhla/Surajpur regional wetland connections.
- **Yamuna is within the larger Ganga drainage system**. Practice key's absolute “not Ganga Basin” is overdrawn: distinguish the immediate **Yamuna sub-basin** from the overarching Ganga basin.
- January **NGT** direction for State's wetland-notification status in **four weeks**; direction/proposal **does not itself notify the wetland or designate a Ramsar site**. **Important Bird Area ≠ Ramsar designation**.
- Embedded historical graphic: identification **2014**, Centre sought Ramsar proposal **2019**; State forest proposal **January 2022**, consent issue **February**, **YEIDA NOC for 112 ha, June 2022**. Those steps precede the January 2025 status inquiry; retain chronology without assuming final approval.
## Birds and ecology
- Marsh habitat important for **Sarus crane, Antigone antigone**, **world's tallest flying bird**, source IUCN **Vulnerable**.
- Three recognised living regional subspecies: **Indian, Eastern, Australian**; Indian is generally largest/heaviest. IUCN threatened category differs from the legal status of a particular wetland.
- Source birds: **common teal, mallard, northern pintail, greylag/bar-headed geese; woolly-necked, black-necked and painted storks; Eurasian marsh harrier**. Great Indian Bustard is principally dry grassland/semi-arid habitat, not this marsh's flagship.
- Protect habitat, drainage, water quality and feeding/breeding areas; land-use/airport development requires transparent assessment and bird/habitat safeguards.

topics.title: Typhon missile system and regional deterrence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Ground-launched system
- **US Army Mid-Range Capability (MRC), Typhon**, **Lockheed Martin system integration**; mobile ground launchers, operations/command centre and reload/support vehicles; reported battery **four launchers**.
- Fires **SM-6 and Tomahawk**; missiles are associated with **Raytheon**, which differs from identifying the Typhon system integrator. [Manufacturer account](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/en-us/news/features/2023/keeping-the-us-army-ahead-of-ready-with-next-generation-launch-systems.html).
- **SM-6** has naval air/surface roles; **Tomahawk** cruise missile has land-attack and maritime variants. A missile's broader family roles **do not prove this deployed Army configuration provides every naval air-defence function**.
- Source **500 km SM-6 / 2,500 km Tomahawk** are reported variant-dependent estimates, not universal official ranges. **Patriot is a different system**, not a Typhon round; ground launcher is not submarine-launch infrastructure.
## January 2025 context
- Reported relocation **within Philippines** to improve mobility/survivability; Chinese/Russian objections and regional deterrence debate. Distinguish relocation from first deployment or a transfer of US missiles into Philippine ownership.
- Regional security balance versus escalation/host-country concerns; deployable strike capability differs from a standing military alliance's political commitments.

topics.title: Eurodrone and India’s observer status
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Programme identity
- **Medium Altitude Long Endurance Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (MALE RPAS)**; **Germany, France, Italy, Spain**, managed by **OCCAR—Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation**, Germany lead nation.
- Industrial prime **Airbus Defence and Space, Germany**; partners **Dassault Aviation, France; Leonardo, Italy; Airbus Spain**. **UK is not one of the four programme States**.
- **21 January 2025, India observer status**, joining Japan as an observer; **observer ≠ full programme partner, procurement order or operational deployment**. [OCCAR programme announcements](https://occar.int/news?cat=13).
## Planned capability
- **Twin-turboprop**, maximum mission payload **2.3 tonnes excluding fuel**, endurance **up to 40 hours** under relevant configuration/conditions. Maximum payload and maximum endurance need not occur simultaneously.
- **ISTAR = intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition, reconnaissance**, possible maritime missions; source ASW/early-warning roles require appropriate mission sensors/configuration, not automatic capability of any airframe.
- Designed with **civil-airspace integration/certification** in mind; manufacturer's superiority/first claims are promotional comparisons, not universal proof. [Airbus specification](https://www.airbus.com/en/products-services/defence/uas/eurodrone).
- European capability/industrial autonomy and reduced reliance on imported Reaper/Heron platforms; India's observation supports familiarity and cooperation without implying a signed purchase.

topics.title: KaWaCHaM and last-mile disaster warnings
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Kerala system
- **Kerala Warnings Crisis and Hazards Management System**, **KaWaCHaM**, Malayalam shield; functional **1 April 2024**, formally inaugurated **21 January 2025**.
- **National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project**, NDMA/World Bank-supported early-warning infrastructure; **NCRMP is a programme, not a separate international funding organisation**. [Kerala SDMA](https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/kawacham/).
- **126 sirens**, strobe lights/cameras, public-building/tower/school sites; source **eight loudspeakers**, reach **up to 1,200 m**, lights **red/orange/yellow**. Reach depends on terrain/noise and must not be mistaken for guaranteed audibility everywhere.
## Warning to action
