- Inputs from **IMD, INCOIS, CWC**, relevant agencies and validated situational reports; social-media information needs verification.
- **State Emergency Operations Centre**, district/local/taluk coordination; multi-hazard alerts for **coastal impacts, intense rain, strong wind, extreme heat**.
- Hazard assessment → authorised alert → siren/voice/light and other channels → evacuation/safe shelter instructions → coordinated response and monitoring.
- Pre-recorded messages, camp/safety information, accessible languages/formats, regular tests and community drills. Source “world's fastest” is not a measured universal ranking; warning value depends on **timely receipt, understanding and action**.

topics.title: Chinar trees and digital heritage conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Tree identity
- **Platanus orientalis, Oriental plane**, family **Platanaceae**; Kashmir **Booun/Boueen**, J&K heritage/state tree.
- **Maple-like leaves do not make it an Acer maple**; poplars are also a different group. Source's “only Platanaceae species in India” needs cultivated/native scope rather than an exhaustive botanical claim.
- Large spreading **deciduous** tree, around **30 m** height, old trunks **10–15 m girth** in source; green summer foliage → red/amber/yellow autumn. Growth **30–50 years to mature height / ~150 full size** is approximate/site-dependent.
- Cultural links to landscape, literature, **papier-mâché/embroidery/wood carving**; source Bhavani-associated local-name tradition and Persian **“che na(r) ast”** etymology are traditions, not verified sole origins.
- Timber/lacewood for furniture; source traditional leaf/bark use and dye-making from twigs/roots are **reported uses, not clinical efficacy claims**.
## Tree Aadhaar
- **J&K Forest Research Institute/Forest Department** tree census, coordinates and **QR-linked unique ID**, recording **25 parameters** such as location, estimated age, girth/height and health.
- January clipping: **28,560 surveyed/geotagged**, estimated regional total **32,000–33,000**, Kashmir and Chenab region; interim census estimates, not all surveyed on a single day.
- Monitor health/removal risks, legal protection and changing condition; permissions remain relevant even on private land.
- Source claims some trees **over 1,000 years**: **geotagging records an age estimate; it does not itself date wood or prove that age**. Credible age evidence and repeat inspections matter.

topics.title: Technology clusters, FDI and inclusive urban growth
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Hyderabad example
- January 2025 source describes Google's planned **Hyderabad campus**, **3 million sq ft / 7.3 acres**, billed as its largest outside the US. Embedded graphic projected **early 2026 completion / capacity for 18,000 employees**; projections are not proof construction or hiring was completed.
- **Gachibowli** IT corridor; institutions **ISB, IIIT Hyderabad**; Telangana **TS-iPASS**, industrial project approval/self-certification system, illustrates facilitation alongside infrastructure and skills.
- Source's blanket claims that Amazon, Microsoft and Facebook each have their “largest campus” here require company-specific comparison; Hyderabad is a major cluster without relying on those superlatives.
## Benefits, risks and response
| Channel | Benefit | Conditions / risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Investment + jobs | Construction, IT/services and suppliers | Jobs/capital inflows must be measured; office size alone is not FDI or GDP |
| Knowledge links | R&D, startup collaboration, global networks | Technology transfer is not automatic |
| Urban growth | Transport, housing, services | Congestion, unaffordable housing, water/power demand and construction pollution |
| Sector concentration | Scale and skilled-worker networks | Global downturn/visa exposure; diversify industries |
- Align transit, affordable housing and civic services with expansion; sustainable buildings, reliable utilities, satellite centres where suitable, industry-linked training in **AI/cloud/data**, and university–firm research.
- Source's **$5 trillion by 2025–26** is a dated ambition, not an achieved GDP statistic. Coaching Mains prompt: investment benefits → distribution/infrastructure constraints → sustainable cluster governance.

topics.title: Diplomatic capacity, MEA funding and development partnerships
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Resources behind foreign policy
- Aspirations in the neighbourhood, Global South, Quad, ASEAN engagement and **International Solar Alliance** require missions, trained diplomats, project delivery and policy research. India engages ASEAN; it is not an ASEAN member.
- **FY 2024–25 MEA Budget Estimates: ₹22,154.67 crore**, including missions, cooperation, passport services and other heads; allocation ≠ expenditure. [MEA annual report, finance chapter](https://www.mea.gov.in/Images/CPV/140725MEAAnnualReport2024English.pdf).
- January editorial: roughly **0.4% of Union budget**, committee recommendation **1%**, suggested staged **0.6–0.8%**. These are dated shares/recommendations; compare like-for-like BE/RE/actuals, including reserve transfers.
- Source comparisons: average **4% annual rise, 2017–2023**, later **23% spike**; training **+30%**, missions/training/cultural heads **+7%**, Nalanda/South Asian University **20–22% cuts**. Different heads and comparison bases; not a single uniform change.
## Grants, loans and implementation
- **Grant** need not be repaid; **loan/Line of Credit** creates repayment/project terms. Aid can support hydropower, connectivity and crisis response; repayment risk and delivery delays matter.
- Source snapshots: aid **−10%**, foreign-government loans **+29%**; Bangladesh allocation **₹200 → ₹120 crore**, Sri Lanka **+63%**; Bhutan largest aid recipient. Bangladesh cumulative LoCs **$7.86 billion**, neighbourhood share **45%**: stocks differ from annual budget flows/disbursements.
- Connectivity through **BBIN/BIMSTEC**, energy interdependence and trusted partnerships; competition with China's BRI does not make every project a zero-sum contest.
## Reform priorities
- Expand recruitment/training and regional expertise; coordinate ministries, monitor costs/time/outcomes, assess loans and local needs, protect fiscal priorities.
- **Track 1** official diplomacy; **Track 2** academic/nonofficial dialogue. Fund research, archive digitisation and lawful declassification to improve institutional memory, with appropriate confidentiality safeguards.
- Mains chain: ambitions → capacity gap → prioritised resources → delivery/accountability → durable influence. Source prompts are coaching questions.

topics.title: Child marriage: substantive equality and annulment
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Ages and remedies
- **PCMA 2006, section 2(a)**: child = **female below 18 / male below 21** for marriage. **Majority Act** adulthood generally **18 for both**; source's “men attain majority at 21” confuses marriage age with general majority.
- **Section 3**: child marriage generally **voidable at the child party's option**, not automatically void in every case; specified circumstances under **sections 12/14** differ. A minor applies through guardian/next friend with Child Marriage Prohibition Officer.
- Section 3(3) allows filing before completing **two years after attaining majority**; interpretation of male limitation has been contested. [Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2055/4/a2007-06.pdf).
## Judgment: reasoning versus outcome
- **T. Sivakumar (Madras HC, 2011)** interpreted male filing limit as **23**; **Independent Thought (SC, 2017)** includes observations relevant to that approach.
- **Sanjay Chaudhary v Guddan, Allahabad HC, 25 October 2024** reasoned for an equal majority-based limit and questioned advantage to adult men. **However, its final decision followed binding Supreme Court precedent, accepted this man's filing before 23 and allowed the appeal**. The PDF's “rejected extension” does not capture that outcome. [Court's published judgment, paragraphs 69–76](https://allahabadhighcourt.in/ILR/ilr-2024/Oct2024.pdf).
- Do not treat the discussion as a nationwide enacted rule abolishing the male 23-year interpretation.
## Substantive equality debate
- **2021 Amendment Bill** proposed women's marriage age **21**; lapsed with dissolution of the 17th Lok Sabha. Proposal ≠ enacted amendment.
- Higher common age: potential schooling, delayed pregnancy and formal equality; concerns: adult **18–21** autonomy, privacy, selective enforcement and criminalisation of consensual relationships.
- Source **49.4% self-initiated marriages**, Enfold/Civic Data Lab 2024 study: sample-specific, not a national prevalence estimate.
- Options debated: equal age **18**, clearer/equal extended annulment periods, accessible legal aid and timely courts. Suggested **3–5 years** is a reform proposal.
- Pair protection from forced marriage with education through 18, livelihoods/social security, safe healthcare/contraception, sexuality education, counselling and survivor support. Formal equal wording must deliver real agency and access to remedies.

topics.title: Milk, dairy cooperatives and nutritional inequality
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Production does not ensure access
- India is the world's largest milk producer; **White Revolution / Operation Flood**, cooperative organisation and **Verghese Kurien** transformed supply and rural livelihoods.
- Milk supplies protein, calcium and micronutrients in many diets; nutritional security also needs dietary diversity, safe food and access. Milk is not compulsory for every person or suitable for every age/allergy.
- January editorial consumption estimates: richest decile **3–4 times** poorest decile; poorest **30% of households consume 18%**. Household surveys can miss consumption outside home; estimates are not the same as national per-capita availability.
- Higher consumption examples **Rajasthan/Punjab/Haryana**, lower **Chhattisgarh/Odisha/West Bengal**; affordability, regional diets and access matter. Source **300 g/day** is a dietary reference, not a universal entitlement.
## Inclusive nutrition policy
- Prioritise children, pregnant/lactating women and vulnerable elderly; locally appropriate supplementary nutrition under **POSHAN/Anganwadi services (ICDS)**. Existing programmes do not guarantee universal daily milk everywhere.
- Reliable State funding, cold chains, quality testing, diversified nutrition, SHG/community engagement; CSR/social bonds are proposed financing additions, not substitutes for public accountability.
- Avoid excess sugar in flavoured milk/processed foods; food choice, lactose intolerance and allergies need consideration. Overnutrition cannot be inferred merely from a person's income.
- Mains: production success → unequal consumption → affordability/service gaps → targeted access and monitoring.
## Question-label caution
- Printed **2012/2018 Prelims** dairy questions and **2014–2023 Mains** list lack confirmed official matches; held for review. The alleged **2019 PM Matsya Sampada** question is especially suspect because the scheme launched in 2020. Do not memorise these as verified PYQs or accept the milk-availability comparison without a year/source.

topics.title: DR Congo: critical minerals and the resource curse
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Map and minerals
- **Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), capital Kinshasa**, Central Africa; distinguish **Republic of Congo, Brazzaville**. Neighbours: **Angola, Zambia, Tanzania, Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, South Sudan, Central African Republic, Republic of Congo**; short Atlantic outlet.
| Mineral | Main use / issue |
| --- | --- |
| Cobalt | Many EV/lithium-ion cathodes; aerospace alloys; not every battery chemistry uses cobalt |
| Copper | Wiring, grids, motors |
| Coltan, columbite–tantalite | Tantalum/niobium ore; tantalum capacitors |
| Gold / diamonds | Jewellery, investment / industrial uses; illicit trade risks |
| Tin / tungsten | Solder / hard alloys and specialist industries |
- Source roughly **70% of world cobalt output**; **2023 PYQ says about three-fourths**. Production shares are dated, not fixed reserves or a prediction.
## Conflict and supply chains
- January 2025 eastern DRC conflict around **Goma**, M23 advances; other armed actors include **ADF and Mai-Mai**. Distinguish eastern conflict-mineral networks from all copper/cobalt mines across DRC.
- External ownership, smuggling, weak revenue governance and armed-group finance can create a **resource curse**: wealth fails to deliver welfare. Child labour/unsafe artisanal mining, displacement, forest loss and water/soil pollution require safeguards.
- China-linked firms have major mining/processing interests; US/EU seek diversified clean-tech supply. Responsible Indian partnerships need due diligence and community benefit.
- **Dodd–Frank section 1502** concerns **tin, tantalum, tungsten, gold (3TG)** and covered issuers' disclosure/due diligence; not a generic ban on all DRC minerals or automatic inclusion of cobalt.
- Transparency **EITI**, traceability, accountable royalties, responsible sourcing, regional/UN cooperation, value addition and economic diversification.
## PYQ recall
- **2023** cobalt: DRC **(c)**; Congo Basin country: Cameroon **(a)**. The latter question's other options are Nigeria/South Sudan/Uganda; answer should not imply Uganda is one of the six commonly listed Congo Basin forest countries.
- **2022** news-pairs: Guinea, Lebanon and Tunisia correctly matched; Chad–Chinese permanent base wrong → **only three pairs (c)**.

topics.title: NavIC, NVS-02 and satellite navigation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Navigation fundamentals
- **NavIC, Navigation with Indian Constellation**, previously **IRNSS**; regional **position/velocity/time** services over India and roughly **1,500 km beyond**.
- Original architecture **7 satellites: 3 geostationary + 4 inclined geosynchronous**. All geostationary orbits are geosynchronous; inclined ones do not stay above one ground point. Design count ≠ number healthy/operational on any date.
- **SPS** civilian and **Restricted Service** authorised/strategic; stated service-area accuracy **better than 20 m**, timing **better than 40 ns**, under specified conditions.
- Other systems: **GPS—US; GLONASS—Russia; Galileo—EU; BeiDou—China; QZSS—Japan**. Interoperability ≠ all systems having identical coverage.
## January 29 launch and later clarification
- **GSLV-F15** inserted **NVS-02**, second NVS-series satellite, into intended **geosynchronous transfer orbit**, on **29 January 2025**, **100th launch from Sriharikota** (not ISRO's 100th mission overall).
- GSLV three stages, indigenous upper cryogenic stage; **Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Andhra Pradesh**. Agency established **15 August 1969**, roots in **INCOSPAR 1962**, Bengaluru HQ.
- Source **1979 SLV-3 experimental flight** failed to reach orbit; first successful SLV-3 orbital launch **18 July 1980**. Sriharikota launch history is wider than SLV-3 alone.
- **2 February 2025 ISRO update**: launch successful, but oxidiser valves did not open for orbit raising; satellite in elliptical orbit, alternative strategies considered. Launch insertion ≠ operational placement in final slot. [ISRO mission and update](https://www.isro.gov.in/GSLV-F15_NVS-02_Mission.html).
## PYQ traps
- **2023** own satellite-navigation system among Australia/Canada/Israel/Japan → **Japan (d)**.
- **2018 IRNSS**: statement 1 correct; **5,500 sq km** boundary claim and promised worldwide coverage by mid-2019 wrong → **1 only (a)**, correcting source key **(b)**.
- Printed **2007 Galileo**: EU multi-satellite navigation project; full official wording/year retained for verification before JSON inclusion.

topics.title: Critical minerals, processing and supply-chain security
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Criticality and uses
- Critical = economic/strategic importance plus supply vulnerability; lists vary by country/time. Mineral occurrence, inferred **resource**, economically recoverable **reserve**, mined output and refining capacity are different.
| Mineral / material | Uses |
| --- | --- |
| Lithium, cobalt, nickel | Many battery chemistries; chemistry-specific demand |
| Graphite | Common lithium-ion anodes |
| Neodymium, dysprosium | Permanent magnets for some EV motors/wind turbines |
| Copper | Electricity networks/electronics |
| Vanadium | Steel alloys / flow batteries |
| Aluminium | Transport/construction/aerospace; strategic use alone does not automatically put it on India's critical list |
- China's extraction and especially processing concentration creates exposure; it does **not** dominate mining of every mineral. DRC cobalt and Australia/lithium-brine countries illustrate different mining locations.
- India has **rare-earth-bearing monazite and other mineral resources**; source's blanket absence of domestic rare earths/cobalt/lithium is misleading. Reasi lithium **inferred resource** is not an operating mine or proven commercial reserve; unverified Rajasthan reserve headlines require caution.
## Response across the value chain
- Explore and assess geology; efficient permitting with social/environmental safeguards; domestic refining/separation and skilled workforce; diversify contracts/overseas assets; strategic stockpiles; recycling/e-waste recovery and material substitution.
- **29 January 2025 NCMM approval**, **2024–25 to 2030–31**: government outlay **₹16,300 crore**, expected PSU/other investment **₹18,000 crore**. Cover exploration → mining → processing → recovery, including overseas partnerships and reserves. Expected investment ≠ public budget already spent. [Cabinet release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2097309&lang=2&reg=48).
- **30 minerals** identified in India's 2023 report; legal schedule categories and that policy list are distinct. FTAs/Quad cooperation can support access, but source's January discussion of EU FTA should not be read as an agreement then in force.
## Beach minerals and PYQs
- **Ilmenite / rutile → titanium**; **monazite → rare earths + thorium**, not present in all Indian coastal sand. **2023 titanium (d)**; **2022 monazite statements 1,2,4 (b)**.
- Monazite's radioactivity invokes special controls; question's legal position is tied to exam year. Source's lithium question labelled 2023 has no confirmed paper match and is held for review.

topics.title: Major and minor minerals: classification and map recall
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Legal distinction
- **MMDR Act 1957, section 3(e)** defines minor minerals: building stones, gravel, ordinary clay, ordinary sand except prescribed uses, and others notified by Centre. It is a **legal classification**, not simply low output/value or a small mine. [Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20096/1/a1957-67.pdf).
- State rules regulate minor-mineral concessions under **section 15**; central notification determines additional minor minerals. Source's attribution solely to **MCR 1960** and inclusion of all gemstones/asbestos as minor are unreliable; diamond is not minor just because it is a gemstone.
- **As at January 2025** mica/quartz/barytes were minor. **20 February 2025 notification** subsequently moved **barytes, felspar, mica, quartz to major**; preserve that date when revising. [Ministry announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2105215&lang=2&reg=48).
## Mineral–location–use recall
| Mineral | Key examples | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coal | Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, MP, Telangana | Power/steel |
| Iron ore | Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Goa | Steel |
| Bauxite | Odisha, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh | Aluminium |
| Manganese | Odisha, MP, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka | Steel/batteries |
| Limestone | Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, AP, Gujarat | Cement/flux |
| Copper | Rajasthan–Khetri; MP–Malanjkhand; Jharkhand–Singhbhum | Conductors |
| Gold | Karnataka–Hutti; AP and other occurrences | Jewellery/investment |
| Lead/zinc | Rajasthan, including Zawar | Batteries/galvanising |
| Salt | Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, AP | Food/chemical industry |
| Chromite | Odisha–Sukinda | Stainless-steel ferrochrome |
| Mica | Jharkhand/Bihar/Rajasthan | Insulation/electronics |
| Marble | Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat | Decorative stone |
| Barytes | AP–Mangampeta | Drilling-fluid weighting |
- Sand/gravel construction; clay bricks/tiles; kaolin ceramics; talc cosmetics/filler; garnet abrasive/filter; quartz glass/electronics; chalk writing/industry; perlite expanded volcanic glass for horticulture/insulation. Asbestos fibres pose serious inhalation hazards; industrial use does not imply safety.
- State lists indicate important examples/occurrences, not exclusive locations, present mining status or equal production shares.

topics.title: Fiscal Health Index and State finances
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Index structure
- **NITI Aayog, inaugural FHI 2025**, released **24 January 2025** by 16th Finance Commission chair; covers **18 major States**, using **FY 2022–23** and CAG data, not every State/UT or the current fiscal year. [Release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2095974&lang=2&reg=48).
| Pillar | Recall indicators |
| --- | --- |
| Quality of expenditure | Development/capital spending; social/economic services |
| Revenue mobilisation | Own tax/non-tax revenue and own-revenue financing |
| Fiscal prudence | Fiscal/revenue deficit patterns |
| Debt index | Debt burden and interest commitments |
| Debt sustainability | Growth–interest relation and debt trajectory |
## FY 2022–23 ranking in 2025 report
- **Achievers**: Odisha **67.8**, Chhattisgarh **55.2**, Goa **53.6**, Jharkhand **51.6**, Gujarat **50.5**.
- **Front-runners**: Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka.
- **Performers**: Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana.
- **Aspirational**: Kerala **25.4**, West Bengal **21.8**, Andhra Pradesh **20.9**, Punjab **10.7**; latter worst, Haryana **27.4** just above this group.
- Report-relative category ≠ permanent State label. Improve own revenues, expenditure quality and credible debt management; comparisons need structural context, not a single rank.
- Practice trap: 18 major States / CAG / five pillars, not all UTs or exclusively Finance Ministry data. Index source year matters when later editions are added.

topics.title: Pangsau Pass, Stilwell Road and border culture
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and heritage
- **Patkai Hills, India–Myanmar border**, near **Nampong, Changlang district, Arunachal Pradesh**; source altitude about **1,136 m / 3,727 ft**. Named after nearby Myanmar village Pangsau.
- Route connects Assam plains toward Myanmar; **Lake of No Return** lies on Myanmar side. Difficult terrain gave nicknames **Hell Pass / Hell Gate**.
- Associated with the reputed route of **13th-century Ahom migration into Assam**, not an independently proved modern border route for every historical account.
- **World War II Stilwell/Ledo Road**, associated with General **Joseph “Vinegar Joe” Stilwell**, connected Allied supply routes toward China after Japanese occupation of Burma.
- **Pangsau Pass International Festival**, Nampong: India–Myanmar cultural contact, tourism and trade; source calls it annual, but recurrence does not prove it was held uninterrupted every year.
- Map recall: Arunachal → Patkai border pass → Myanmar → Lake of No Return; not Western Ghats/Aravallis.

topics.title: Blue carbon and coastal wetland protection
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Carbon storage
- Carbon captured/stored by ocean/coastal ecosystems; key **coastal vegetated sinks: mangroves, salt marshes, seagrass meadows**. Carbon stored in vegetation and especially sediments. [NOAA](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/bluecarbon.html).
- Source's **10-times terrestrial-forest rate** describes a comparison of relevant coastal habitats, not a universal rate for all oceans/reefs or equal carbon stocks everywhere.
- Coral reefs are biodiversity-rich but **not included among the standard three coastal blue-carbon habitats** in the practice question; carbon sequestration and carbonate formation differ.
## Services and threats
- Climate mitigation + coastal protection + nurseries/fisheries/food security + adaptation.
- Conversion for aquaculture/agriculture, destructive harvesting, pollution and urban/industrial reclamation threaten stored carbon and livelihoods; degradation may release carbon.
- Protect existing habitats, restore suitable hydrology, prevent pollution and measure long-term carbon/benefits; poorly placed plantations do not replace functioning seagrass or marsh ecosystems.

topics.title: Deep Ocean Mission and Samudrayaan
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission and components
- **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, multi-institutional Central Sector mission, Cabinet-approved **2021**, estimated **₹4,077 crore**, two phases over initial **2021–2026** period.
- Six components: **deep-sea mining/submersible/robotics; ocean climate advisories; biodiversity exploration/conservation technology; deep-ocean survey; ocean energy/freshwater; advanced marine station for ocean biology**.
- **Samudrayaan** manned-submersible component: **Matsya 6000**, intended **three people to 6,000 m**, scientific sensors. Design/testing milestone ≠ completed crewed 6-km operational dive.
- Supports **blue economy** knowledge/technology; living and non-living resource assessment must consider fragile deep-sea habitats, sediment plumes and international rules.
- Graphic contrasts shallow human diving and deep engineering; pressure rises with depth, requiring a strong pressure sphere, life support, communications and recovery systems. Mission is wider than mineral extraction alone.

topics.title: Paraquat: herbicide toxicity and regulation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Toxicity
- **Paraquat**, methyl viologen, commonly paraquat dichloride; herbicide for weeds/grass, also agricultural desiccation in permitted uses. Not a fertiliser.
- **WHO hazard Class II**, source “moderately hazardous”; classification does **not** make swallowing safe. Regulatory restriction differs from a toxicological class.
- Ingestion can cause severe mouth/GI injury and lung, kidney, liver/heart damage, seizures and respiratory failure. Longer/stronger skin exposure, especially broken skin, can poison; inhalation/eye exposure also harms. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/chemical-emergencies/chemical-fact-sheets/paraquat.html).
- **No proven antidote/cure**; urgent specialist treatment and supportive care. Source mentions charcoal haemoperfusion/immunosuppression as clinical approaches, not guaranteed effective cures or self-treatment instructions.
## Regulation and January context
- January 2025 Kerala poisoning-case sentencing brought attention to access and handling; trial judgment ≠ proof appeal outcomes are final.
- Source says banned in **70+ countries**; country counts/date/meaning of ban vary. EU/China restrictions and **US restricted-use licensing** illustrate different regimes; source's “banned in India” practice distractor is false in its January account.
- Safe storage, access control, training, labelling and poisoning surveillance matter; occupational and intentional exposures require distinct prevention measures.

topics.title: Titan arum: corpse-flower pollination
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identity and life cycle
- **Amorphophallus titanum**, correcting PDF **“titanium”**; Titan arum / **Bunga bangkai**, native to **Sumatra, Indonesia**, IUCN **Endangered**. January Sydney flowering specimen **Putricia** drew large crowds.
- **Inflorescence**, not one giant individual flower: **spadix** bears many small flowers, enclosed by a purple **spathe**. May reach about **3 m**; bloom brief, roughly **24–48 hours**, interval variable and sometimes many years.
- Underground **corm** stores energy built through leaf cycles; bloom needs adequate reserves, not a fixed once-yearly/once-decade clock.
- Female flowers receptive **before male pollen release**, reducing self-pollination; carrion smell/heat attracts **flies and beetles**, encouraging pollen transfer. [US Botanic Garden](https://www.usbg.gov/gardens-plants/corpse-flowers).
- Source volatile list: **dimethyl disulfide/trisulfide, methanethiol, methyl thioacetate, 3-methylbutanal, isovaleric acid**; odour is a mixture, not a single compound.
- Botanical propagation/pollen exchange helps conserve genetic diversity; rare garden bloom does not imply natural population recovery.

topics.title: IWAI and inland-waterway infrastructure
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution and routes
- **Inland Waterways Authority of India Act 1985**; IWAI established **27 October 1986**, HQ **Noida**, **Ports, Shipping and Waterways Ministry**. Develops/maintains navigation infrastructure on national waterways.
- **23 January 2025**, Varanasi sub-office upgraded to Regional Office for **NW-1, Ganga** and Uttar Pradesh waterways; sixth Regional Office alongside **Guwahati, Patna, Kochi, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata** in source snapshot. [Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2095758&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source jurisdiction: **Betwa, Chambal, Gomti, Tons, Varuna**, parts of **Gandak, Ghaghra, Karamnasa, Yamuna**, coordination with UP State IWT Authority. Naming a river ≠ every reach already commercially navigable.
- Benefit depends on fairway depth, terminals, last-mile freight, seasonal flows and ecological safeguards; inland shipping is not automatically feasible on every tributary.

topics.title: White-naped tit and dry scrub habitat
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification
- **Machlolophus nuchalis**, family **Paridae**, passerine; endemic to India, source IUCN **Vulnerable**.
- Disjunct northwestern (**Gujarat/Rajasthan and source Haryana**) and southern (**AP/Karnataka/Tamil Nadu**) distribution; **dry thorn scrub** habitat.
- Black upperparts, white nape/upper-mantle patch, white cheeks/underparts with central black band, white wing patch; pairs/small groups, identifiable calls.
- January report first documented occurrence in **Kappatagudda hills, North Karnataka**; new local record ≠ new species or first record anywhere in Karnataka.
- Habitat loss/fragmentation matters; do not substitute wetland/evergreen-rainforest habitat in recall questions.

topics.title: Epicoccum indicum and plant-pathogenic fungi
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Discovery and plant disease
- Source reports **Epicoccum indicum**, **Ascomycota, Didymellaceae**, associated with emerging **leaf spot of vetiver, Chrysopogon zizanioides**, studied by **Banaras Hindu University** researchers; name refers to India.
- **Phytopathogenic fungi** cause plant disease/economic loss; roots, stems, leaves, flowers and fruits can be affected. Fungal enzymes can break cell-wall carbohydrate polymers.
- **Necrotroph** kills tissue and feeds on it; **biotroph** feeds on living tissue. Many plant-pathogenic fungi lie in Ascomycota/Basidiomycota; not all fungi are pathogenic.
- Leaf spots are a symptom group, often fungal but sometimes bacterial; colour/size/shape vary, severe disease reduces plant health.
- Source **70–80% of plant diseases** is a broad textbook estimate, not a measured proportion for every crop or region. Association, experimental pathogenicity and global disease prevalence are different claims.

topics.title: Pinaka rocket artillery and ammunition procurement
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System and roles
- Indigenous **Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher / MLRS**, developed by **DRDO–ARDE** for Indian Army; Army is user, not sole designer.
- **Two pods × six rockets**, mobile truck launcher with stabilising outriggers; loader/replenishment vehicles and command post. **214 mm** basic rocket, source payload about **100 kg**, differing warheads.
- Area targets: exposed troops, vehicles, communications, airfield facilities and ammunition/fuel dumps; pre-fragmented high explosive and area-denial rounds have different effects. Artillery rocket system ≠ surface-to-air defence.
- Basic Mk-I commonly cited around **38 km**; enhanced/guided rounds extend range/accuracy. Source's inconsistent **48/60/90 km** version table, **48-second** salvo and exact **5,757.70 km/h Mk-3** should not be learned as universal specifications. Launcher commonly cited **12 rounds in ~44 seconds**; launcher versus six-launcher battery differs.
- January source describes enhanced HE **45 km**, area-denial **37 km**, guided developments about **75 km**, future **120/300 km** ambitions. Planned variants ≠ then-operational capability, and “air attacks” is misleading.
## January approval and contract distinction
- January **CCS** approval reported near **₹10,000 crore**, source approximate splits **₹6,050 / ₹4,000 crore**, signing expected by March. Approval ≠ contract signed or ammunition delivered.
- Correct **MIL = Munitions India Limited**, not **Mishra Dhatu Nigam (MIDHANI)**. Private supplier **Economic Explosives Limited (EEL), Solar group**.
- **6 February 2025 clarification**: MoD signed rocket contracts totalling **₹10,147 crore** with EEL/MIL; **BEL SHAKTI software upgrade** also contracted. [MoD release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2100335&lang=2&reg=3).
- Domestic ammunition capacity, logistics/replenishment, credible delivery schedules and quality trials support readiness; higher volume/range alone does not prove precision or eliminate escalation concerns.

topics.title: Sodium reduction and potassium-enriched salt substitutes
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## WHO guidance and mechanism
- **27 January 2025 WHO guideline**: adults should consume **less than 2 g sodium/day ≈ 5 g salt**, from all dietary sources; sodium mass ≠ salt mass.
- If using table salt, conditional recommendation to replace regular salt with **lower-sodium substitutes containing potassium**, within an overall reduction strategy. Not encouragement to increase salt intake. [Guideline](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240105591).
- Intended for general adult population; **excludes pregnant women, children and people with kidney impairment/other impaired potassium excretion**. Not simply “safe for everyone except known kidney disease”.
- Excess sodium raises blood pressure and cardiovascular risk; substituting potassium may lower pressure. Source's direct sodium → fatty-plaque claim oversimplifies atherosclerosis; reduced salt is not a proven cure for diabetes.
## India and implementation
- Source estimates **10.4 g salt/day** in India and cites **1.9 million global deaths** associated with excess sodium; dated estimates, not identical to each person's intake/risk.
- Food added at table/cooking and processed snacks all matter. **Hyperkalaemia** risk requires appropriate clinical assessment, especially kidney disease and relevant medicines; screening/clear labels and public-health counselling.
- Affordable products, industry sodium reduction, accurate nutrient claims, education through health workers/SHGs and monitoring of intake/outcomes; price subsidy/display mandates are source proposals, not enacted requirements.
- Source edible-salt **97% NaCl** specification must not be mechanically applied to every salt substitute. **2.2%** refers to water-insoluble-matter provision in relevant standards; not a blanket limit on all anti-caking agents. [FSSAI additives compendium](https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Food_Additives_Regulations_26_03_2021.pdf).
- Sodium reduction and iodine sufficiency must be considered together; replacing a food ingredient does not automatically preserve iodine delivery.

topics.title: Leprosy: transmission, treatment and stigma
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease and diagnosis
- **Hansen disease**, mainly **Mycobacterium leprae**, bacterial; affects skin, **peripheral nerves**, eyes and upper-respiratory mucosa. Pale/discoloured patches with reduced sensation, nerve weakness, ulcers and advanced deformity/eye damage.
- Spread usually prolonged close contact with untreated disease, respiratory droplets; not highly contagious, not ordinary casual contact. Incubation averages about **5 years**, may extend **20+ years**; source “5–20” is not a strict minimum/maximum.
- Clinical cardinal signs and nerve assessment guide diagnosis; slit-skin smear/biopsy where needed. **Lepromin test does not diagnose active infection**.
| Treatment category | Recall | MDT duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paucibacillary (PB) | Usually 1–5 lesions, no demonstrated bacilli | **6 months** |
| Multibacillary (MB) | >5 lesions, nerve involvement or smear bacilli as per criteria | **12 months** |
- **Rifampicin + clofazimine + dapsone**, curable with MDT; early treatment prevents disability. Contact screening and eligible **single-dose rifampicin post-exposure prophylaxis** add prevention. [WHO](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/leprosy).
## India: elimination is not eradication
- National public-health elimination **2005**, prevalence **<1/10,000**; new cases/local transmission persist. **NLEP 1983**, **SPARSH** awareness, **Nikusth 2.0** surveillance and **NSP/Roadmap 2023–27**, source ambition **zero transmission by 2027**—target, not achievement. [2023 announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleasepage.aspx?lang=2&prid=1909081&reg=48).
- PB three-drug revision issued **17 January 2024**, Indian implementation from **1 April 2025**; source's January wording should not imply already implemented everywhere. Nikusth 2.0 launched **30 January 2023**. [Programme chronology](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2174943&lang=2&reg=3).
- January source focus **124 districts**, Bihar/Chhattisgarh/Jharkhand/Maharashtra/Odisha; broader high-burden list includes UP/West Bengal/MP. **53.6% global cases, 2021–22**, **~60%, 2023**, **~9% children** refer to different periods/denominators, not one current statistic.
- Stigma, hidden cases, delayed care, disability and remote/tribal access need trained primary care, rehabilitation, anti-discrimination and community participation.
- WHO **2021–2030** global strategy, ILEP partners; BCG offers some protection but routine BCG programme is not a dedicated guaranteed leprosy vaccine. Free MDT is distinct from general health-insurance coverage.

topics.title: Ad hoc High Court judges and Article 224A
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional mechanism
- **Article 224A**: High Court Chief Justice, with **President's previous consent**, may request a retired judge of that or another High Court to sit/act; judge's consent required. Entitled to relevant judicial powers while sitting; temporary remedy, not a permanent appointment under Article 217.
- Distinguish **Article 224** additional/acting judges and Supreme Court **Article 127** ad hoc judges; **224A concerns retired High Court judges**.
## January 30, 2025 order
- **Lok Prahari v Union of India**, modification of **20 April 2021** guidelines to address large criminal-appeal backlog.
- Original safeguard: do not resort to ad hoc appointments unless **80% of sanctioned strength already working or recommended**. January order kept that condition in abeyance; source's description “only when vacancies crossed 20%” reverses this prerequisite.
- **2–5 ad hoc judges per High Court**, **not above 10% of sanctioned strength**; sit with serving judges on **Division Benches for criminal appeals** under the January arrangement. Later orders may clarify bench deployment; do not make the temporary direction timeless.
- Source pendency roughly **60+ lakh**, **20 lakh criminal appeals**, January snapshot; not current totals. [Supreme Court institutional account](https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3ec0490f1f4972d133619a60c30f3559e/uploads/2025/05/2025051413.pdf).
## Benefits and safeguards
- Experienced judges can reduce older appeals and delay; appointments need transparent suitability/consent, logistics, Registry support and independence.
- Not a substitute for filling regular vacancies, case management and adequate court infrastructure; criminal appeal disposal is distinct from clearing every pending trial.
- Practice recall **224A (b)**; source question has no PYQ year and remains coaching practice.
## Judicial administration discussion: February 2025
- Conference emphasis: identify backlog categories, regular judicial officer/prosecutor recruitment, sufficient infrastructure and **permanent IT/data support cadres**.
- Objective transfers, transparent merit-based district-judge elevation, case management and reliable pendency data can improve access to justice under **Article 21**.
- These are reform discussions/proposals, not newly enacted national appointment rules; maintain judicial independence, data protection and accessibility while digitising.

topics.title: Economic Survey 2024–25: indicators and policy signals
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Purpose
- Annual economic assessment prepared by **Department of Economic Affairs, Finance Ministry**, led by **Chief Economic Adviser**; usually presented before Union Budget. Policy recommendations are advisory, not spending authorisation.
- First Survey **1950–51**, separated from Budget **1964**. Chapter structure/statistical appendix can vary; “Part A/Part B” is not a permanent constitutional rule.
## Read each indicator with its period
| Indicator | Survey snapshot |
| --- | --- |
| Real GDP | **6.4% FY2024–25 first advance estimate**; **6.3–6.8% FY2025–26 projection** |
| Retail inflation | **5.4% FY2023–24 → 4.9% April–December 2024** |
| Bank gross NPAs | **2.6%, September 2024** |
| Gross FDI inflows | **US$55.6 billion, April–November 2024**, +17.9%; not net FDI or full-year total |
| Total exports | Merchandise + services **+6%, April–December 2024** |
| Services share of GVA | **55.3% FY2024–25 estimate**, versus 50.6% FY2013–14 |
- Infrastructure Union capital expenditure **38.8% trend growth rate, FY2020–FY2024**; not a 38.8% cumulative increase. [Survey overview](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/economicsurvey/doc/eschapter/echap01.pdf), [external-sector chapter](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/economicsurvey/doc/eschapter/echap03.pdf).
- Source industry **6.2% FY2024–25 estimated growth**; electronics **17.5% CAGR FY2015–FY2024**; steel **4.6%**, automobile **12.5% FY2023–24**, and agriculture **~16% GDP FY2023–24** are period-specific figures. GDP share ≠ GVA share; forecasts ≠ eventual outcomes.
- Insurance source **₹11.2 lakh crore / 7.7%** has insufficient segment/period clarity; do not treat it as a verified common total.
## Mains connections
- Private investment and infrastructure → productivity; skilling and employment → inclusive demand; prudent fiscal/financial policy → resilience.
- Disinflation helps purchasing power but aggregate growth need not imply equal household gains. Assess jobs, regional distribution, social outcomes and environmental costs alongside GDP.

topics.title: VSHORADS: portable short-range air defence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System and trial
- **Very Short-Range Air Defence System**, indigenous **MANPADS**, developed by **DRDO Research Centre Imarat** with other laboratories and production partners; close-range defence against low-flying aerial threats.
- **1 February 2025, Chandipur, Odisha**: three trials intercepted high-speed, low-altitude targets with reduced thermal signatures simulating drones. Two field operators performed readiness, acquisition and firing in final deployment configuration. [MoD release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2098784&lang=2&reg=48).
- Infrared homing; source approximate **6 km** range and supersonic flight. Compare **Stinger—US**, **Igla-S—Russia**, but variant-dependent ranges are not fixed universal specifications.
- Designed to meet Army/Navy/Air Force needs; successful development trials **do not establish operational induction in all three services**.
## Strategic significance
- Mobile battlefield/local asset defence, including drone threats; reduced import dependence, domestic production and possible export potential.
- Must integrate detection, identification, command and ammunition supply; not a universal counter to every UAV, swarm or high-altitude aircraft.
- Source defence question is **practice, no verified PYQ year**.

topics.title: Budget 2025–26: income-tax relief and demand
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Proposal and limits
- **1 February 2025 Budget**, FY2025–26 / AY2026–27 new-regime proposals: resident individuals with normal taxable income up to **₹12 lakh** receive rebate; eligible salaried income **₹12.75 lakh** after **₹75,000 standard deduction**.
- **₹12 lakh is a rebate threshold, not the nil-rate slab**. Special-rate income such as capital gains/lottery is excluded from this rebate; marginal relief applies under specified conditions just above threshold. [Income-tax FAQ](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Documents/Budget/budget-2025/faqs-budget-2025.pdf).
| Income slab (₹ lakh) | Marginal rate |
| --- | --- |
| 0–4 | Nil |
| 4–8 | 5% |
| 8–12 | 10% |
| 12–16 | 15% |
| 16–20 | 20% |
| 20–24 | 25% |
| Above 24 | 30% |
- Rates apply to each slab, not the whole income at the highest applicable rate. [Budget highlights](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/bh1.pdf).
- **~₹1 lakh crore direct-tax revenue forgone**, Budget estimate for direct-tax proposals, not proof of an equal deficit increase or realised annual loss. [Budget speech](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/Budget_Speech.pdf).
## Economic transmission
- Tax relief → disposable income → consumption **and/or** savings; consumption can stimulate output/jobs, savings may finance investment. Response depends on income group, confidence, credit and supply capacity.
- Risks: fiscal opportunity cost, imports as leakage, inflation where supply constrained; crowding-in through investment is contingent. Investment does not have a universally larger multiplier in every setting.
- Combine private consumption/investment with effective public spending; judge distribution, employment and revenue outcomes rather than assuming tax cuts always finance themselves.

topics.title: US tariff escalation: implications for India
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## February 2025 sequence
- **1 February** announcement: additional tariffs **25% Canada/Mexico**, **10% China**; Canadian energy **10%** exception. [US announcement](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/02/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-imposes-tariffs-on-imports-from-canada-mexico-and-china/).
- **3 February** Canada/Mexico measures paused for about a month; source discussion precedes this development. [Mexico pause order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/02/progress-on-the-situation-at-our-southern-border/). Rates/coverage are dated policy snapshots, not present-day universal tariffs.
## Channels affecting India
| Opportunity | Constraint/risk |
| --- | --- |
| US buyers diversify from China | Capacity, quality, prices and rules of origin |
| Textiles/electronics/engineering exports | Competitors may also gain; gains not assured |
| China-plus-one investment | Logistics, policy certainty and skilled labour |
| Canada/Mexico alternative markets | Their demand and trade rules still matter |
- US tariff is collected on US imports; **does not mechanically increase the price of Chinese goods imported into India**. Diversion might instead depress prices and intensify competition; supply disruption can raise some costs.
- Standard goods tariffs do not directly apply to IT services in the same manner. Oil prices, dollar strength, portfolio flows and uncertainty create indirect inflation/currency channels.
- Chinese commercial competition, minerals/supply dependence and Indo-Pacific diplomacy require a differentiated response; economic change does not establish military retaliation.
## Policy response
- Strengthen manufacturing, standards, ports and diversified sourcing; evaluate PLI outcomes, not subsidy announcements alone.
- Bilateral dialogue and lawful WTO-consistent trade remedies; anti-dumping requires evidence/investigation, not merely rising imports.
- India's US **GSP benefits removed 2019**; restoration was a negotiating suggestion in source, not an accomplished February reform.

topics.title: Green cardamom: taxonomy and wild relatives
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Botanical recall
- Green/small cardamom **Elettaria cardamomum**, **Zingiberaceae**, humid shaded tropical hills; distinguish large/black cardamom (*Amomum subulatum*).
- **2024 Taxon study** recircumscribes **Elettaria as seven species**: cultivated *E. cardamomum*, four taxa reassigned from *Alpinia* (**ensal, floribunda, involucrata, rufescens**) and two newly described species.
- **E. facifera**—Periyar/Idukki; **E. tulipifera**—Agasthyamalai and Munnar, Kerala source localities. New description ≠ newly evolved plant. [Kew accepted name](https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn%3Alsid%3Aipni.org%3Anames%3A77347899-1), [original taxonomy paper](https://doi.org/10.1002/tax.13242).
- Name traced to old Malayalam **“elletari”**, recorded in **Hortus Malabaricus**, seventeenth-century botanical work.
## Agriculture and conservation
- Wild relatives provide potential genetic resources for resistance/climate adaptation; discovery **does not prove commercial edibility, superior flavour or ready-to-use cultivars**.
- Kerala **Idukki/Wayanad**, Karnataka **Kodagu/Chikkamagaluru**, Tamil Nadu **Nilgiris**: major growing landscapes; rain/heat extremes, pest pressure, cost and volatile prices affect returns.
- Source India “world's largest producer/exporter” claim is wrong: **Guatemala leads global cardamom production**, India is an important producer with strong domestic demand. [National Horticulture Board](https://nhb.gov.in/NHBDPR/Cardamom_DPR.pdf).
- **Malabar/Mysore** are recognised cultivar types; source labels them GI tags without registration evidence. Do not equate a cultivar name with GI status; ₹1,000 crore/100-country export figures lack specified period.
- Spices Board promotes sector/exports; **ICAR–IISR** research. Protect habitats, conserve germplasm, support sustainable shade cultivation/quality branding; SDGs **8,12,15**.

topics.title: Uttarakhand UCC: live-in registration and privacy
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 framework
- Uttarakhand **UCC Act 2024 / Rules 2025**, implemented **27 January 2025**; regulates marriage, divorce, succession and qualifying live-in relationships, with statutory scope/exemptions. **Article 44** is a DPSP, not an independently enforceable fundamental right.
- Live-in category is an adult man and woman living in a shared household in a relationship in the nature of marriage. Existing marriage/live-in partnership, prohibited relationship (subject to lawful custom) and coercion/fraud can bar registration.
- Statement required within **one month**; registrar enquiry and termination reporting. Children recognised as legitimate; abandoned woman can seek maintenance under relevant provisions.
- **Under 21: parents/guardians notified; notification is not a blanket statutory requirement of parental consent for adults**. Source conflates these.
## Registration and penalties
- Rules involve identity/age/residence and shared accommodation documentation, online/offline processing, provisional arrangements and landlord-related obligations; protect documents from needless disclosure.
- Source maximums: non-submission **3 months / ₹10,000 / both**, false statement **3 months / ₹25,000 / both**; failure after registrar's notice has a separate stronger penalty. Check applicable statutory section rather than treating all omissions identically.
- ST/constitutionally protected customary categories exempted; territorial/resident applicability matters, not every person nationwide covered. [State rules](https://www.ucc.uk.gov.in/server/file/uploads/shared-files/ucc-rules-2025-en.pdf).
## Rights analysis
- Potential benefits: evidence for maintenance, protection against abandonment, recognised children and legal clarity.
- Concerns: compulsory intimate-data disclosure, police/parent notification, housing exclusion, data leaks, disproportionate effect on interfaith/inter-caste couples.
- **Article 21**, *Puttaswamy* privacy **2017**: legality, legitimate aim, necessity/proportionality and safeguards; criticism does not mean a court has struck down the law.
- Safeguards: data minimisation, restricted access, secure retention, accessible grievance/appeal process and proportionate enforcement. Source questions are practice with no PYQ year.

topics.title: Rupee depreciation: trade and capital-flow channels
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## February 3 market snapshot
- Source: rupee closed **₹87.17/US$**, down **55 paise**, intraday **₹87.29**; Sensex **77,186.74**, Nifty **23,361.05**. Historical market quotes, not current rates or predictions.
- Dollar index **109.46**, oil-importer dollar demand, foreign portfolio outflow **₹1,327.09 crore**, trade-policy uncertainty and risk aversion contributed; correlation alone cannot quantify each cause.
- Forex reserves **US$629.557 billion**, weekly increase **US$5.574 billion, week ended 24 January 2025**; reserve changes reflect valuation and transactions, not RBI intervention alone.
## Mechanism and trade-offs
- **Depreciation = more rupees for one dollar**. Importers face higher rupee costs; exporters may gain rupee receipts but imported inputs, hedging and weak foreign demand can offset gains.
- Oil/import dependence → possible imported inflation and external-balance pressure; borrowers with unhedged foreign-currency debt face greater repayment burden.
- Indian exchange rate is market determined with RBI volatility management; source **“free-floating”** is too absolute. Intervention can smooth disorderly moves, not guarantee a specific rate indefinitely.
- Source Brent **US$76.74/bbl** and negative rupee outlook are dated observations/forecasts. US tariff announcements and later pauses must be read chronologically.

topics.title: Arunachal Himalayan glaciers: retreat and GLOF risk
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Study and corrected arithmetic
- *Journal of Earth System Science*, **2025**, Ritse/Hazarika/Kulnu/Jamir: Landsat and Sentinel-2A imagery, semi-automatic mapping/GIS, **Randolph Glacier Inventory / GLIMS** reference, **1988–2020** Arunachal Himalayas.
- **756 → 646 glaciers**, net **110 fewer**. Initial area **585.23 ±3.4 km²**; published university abstract gives final area **275.381 ±2.9 km²**, implying loss **309.849 km² ≈52.9%**. Source swaps final area/loss and prints **47%**. [Author institution abstract](https://cottonuniversity.ac.in/index_research_highlights_details?lang=ASM&p=elN5S25McE1zYTRuQm1WcStNYmZmQT09?).
- Abstract also states **16.94 km²/year**, which does **not equal** the simple endpoint average (**309.849/32 ≈9.68 km²/year**). Method/period needs resolution; do not memorise 16.94 as endpoint arithmetic.
- Survey spans Tawang–Lohit, including West Kameng/Kurung Kumey/Upper Siang/Upper Dibang Valley; inventory boundaries and counting fragmented glaciers affect comparisons.
- Source temperature **0.1–0.8°C/decade**, future **5–6°C / precipitation +20–30%** lack scenario/baseline; projections are conditional, not assured forecasts.
## Why retreat matters
- Melting/retreat may form unstable glacial lakes → **GLOF**, threatening settlements, roads and hydropower. Not every glacier loss creates a lake or outburst.
- **2023 South Lhonak–Teesta disaster**, Sikkim, damaged **1,200 MW Teesta III**; source 55 deaths is a dated reported count, not final verified total.
- Changing seasonal runoff affects water security and irrigation; immediate meltwater increase does not guarantee long-term water abundance.
- Monitor lake/glacier change, assess moraine stability, install warning/evacuation systems, use hazard-sensitive infrastructure siting and coordinated catchment planning. Afforestation alone cannot stop glacier retreat/GLOF.

topics.title: Forest diversion, linear projects and compensatory land
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Supreme Court interim direction
- **3 February 2025, Ashok Kumar Sharma v Union of India**, challenges to 2023 forest-law amendment: until further orders, no Union/State steps reducing forest land unless **compensatory land is provided for afforestation**. [Original order](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2023/40155/40155_2023_2_32_59163_Order_03-Feb-2025.pdf).
- Applies to reduction, including relevant linear projects; **not a categorical ban on all roads/railways/pipelines**, nor final invalidation of the whole amendment.
- **T.N. Godavarman 1996** dictionary meaning of forest, ownership/classification irrespective, and recorded forests remain central. Source's “February 2023” interim reference appears confused with **19 February 2024** directions pending consolidated records.
- **Section 1A**, 2023 amendment: statutory coverage of notified and government-recorded forest categories; exceptions and provisos require reading the Act. **Rule 16, 2023 Rules** consolidated State/UT records; source **1.97 lakh km²** estimate is not itself a court-certified universal inventory.
## Conservation versus infrastructure
- Prior statutory approval, applicable environmental safeguards, forest/community rights and compensatory measures are distinct requirements; planting does not automatically authorise diversion.
- New plantation area does **not instantly replace old-growth biodiversity, carbon stocks or livelihoods**.
- Prefer avoidance/alternative alignments, minimise fragmentation, provide wildlife crossings, verify suitable compensatory land, survival/maintenance and transparent compliance monitoring.
- **Articles 48A / 51A(g)** environmental duties and Article 21 jurisprudence; balance public infrastructure need with ecological and rights safeguards.

topics.title: Ethanol blending: maize demand and food–fuel balance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Programme and dated source estimates
- **E20 = 20% ethanol blended petrol**, by volume; policy advanced target to **2025–26** from original 2030. February source forecast “within two months” is not proof then achieved.
- Source annual requirement **~1,100 crore litres**, installed capacity **~1,600 crore litres**: capacity ≠ realised production/OMC procurement or achieved blend.
- Proposed supply: FCI/broken rice **~110 crore litres**, sugar/high-grade molasses **~400**, maize **350–400**; these figures do not sum to total requirement and are not a complete reconciled supply balance.
- Sugar-diversion restrictions increased maize interest; source FCI rice price **₹28 → ₹22.50/kg**, maize **42 million tonnes FY2024–25**, **9 million tonnes** ethanol demand are contemporary estimates/policy context, not final harvest data.
## Supply-chain effects
- Growing States include **Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar, UP**. Stable demand may increase farmer returns but alter acreage and prices for poultry, livestock and starch users.
- Source maize imports **US$33 million FY2023–24 → US$188 million April–November 2024**; unequal periods. April–June ₹100 crore is a separate rupee snapshot.
- **DDGS**, distillers' dried grains with solubles, recovers feed value; not a complete one-for-one substitute for every maize feed formulation.
- Domestic fuel can reduce crude import exposure; source **₹6,000 crore per 100 crore litres** is a scenario-sensitive claim, dependent on petroleum/ethanol prices, energy content and imported inputs.
## Sustainable response
- Diversify suitable feedstocks; cellulosic/second-generation agricultural-residue ethanol, flexible distilleries, fair procurement and transparent stock assessments.
- Assess water use, food/feed prices, land competition and lifecycle emissions; biofuel is not automatically carbon neutral. Ensure engine/fuel compatibility and quality standards.
- Later confirmation: **July 2025 monthly blending ~19.93%**, not evidence February already E20. [Programme chronology](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2283118&lang=1&reg=3).

topics.title: Mental health at work: inclusion of blue-collar workers
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Problem and evidence
- Low pay, insecure work, excessive hours, low control, unsafe conditions and harassment create **psychosocial risks**; informal/blue-collar workers often lack accessible confidential care.
- Source **10.6% adult prevalence / 70–92% treatment gap**, drawn from earlier national survey/Economic Survey discussion, is not a new February 2025 census of workers; condition-specific gaps vary.
- Corporate examples **Infosys HALE, Wipro Mitra, TCS employee assistance** illustrate unequal support, not universal coverage of all white-collar workers.
## Labour-law debate
- **OSHWC Code 2020** employer health/safety duties and **Code on Social Security 2020** employment injury/occupational disease framework need effective psychosocial-risk implementation. Source's categorical “all mental illness excluded” oversimplifies statutory language, causation and coverage.
- Work-related injury claims may involve causation evidence and occupational-disease schedules; a contributory-stress court example is not automatic eligibility for every condition.
- Source March 31, 2025 harmonisation deadline is a reported aim, **not proof all four codes had commenced nationwide** on that date.
## Inclusive policy framework
- Prevent risks through reasonable workload/hours, predictable employment, anti-harassment measures and worker participation; counselling cannot compensate for persistently harmful conditions.
- Train supervisors, offer confidential affordable care and referral/return-to-work support; link **Tele-MANAS**, primary care and rehabilitation.
- Employer–worker–mental-health specialist cooperation; evaluate explicit occupational-disease protection, enforcement, accessible reporting and non-discrimination. These reform proposals are not automatically enacted duties.
- [WHO workplace guideline](https://www.who.int/publications-detail-redirect/9789240053052) supports organisational measures, manager/worker training, interventions and employment/return-to-work support; **SDGs 3 and 8**.
- Source 15-mark question is coaching practice, no verified PYQ year; use mains structure **risk/exclusion → legal gaps → prevention/access/accountability → equitable decent work**.
